capabilities.title: Member chat compression controls
capabilities.summary:
- read my compression settings and what is in effect
- set my compression settings: a master switch plus Tool-result compression, Plain-speak and Prompt trim
- view compression statistics for me and for a conversation I can read
- reset my compression statistics
- compact a conversation I own, with optional guidance, and follow its progress
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
Available by default; each member opts in. `MEMBER_COMPRESSION_ENABLED` defaults to `True` (`src/kaizen/config.py:1886`), and so do the three per-control flags (`src/kaizen/config.py:1887`, `src/kaizen/config.py:1888`, `src/kaizen/config.py:1891`). A member's settings start with everything off (`src/kaizen/domain/compression.py:36`). A control takes effect only when the deployment allows it and the member has turned on both the master switch and that control (`src/kaizen/domain/compression.py:158`). When `MEMBER_COMPRESSION_ENABLED` is off, the settings and statistics routes return not found (`src/kaizen/member/app.py:498`). Administrators can switch it as a live setting (`src/kaizen/admin/catalog.py:242`).

Where the three controls take effect was traced through the Pi agent adapter (`src/kaizen/agents/adapters/pi_core.py:48`, `src/kaizen/agents/adapters/pi_run_loop.py:740`); other agent runtimes were not checked.

What each control does:

- Tool-result compression applies to code-execution output. The sandbox worker runs a pinned RTK pass over captured stdout and stderr and returns the raw output beside a compressed copy (`src/kaizen/sandbox/rpc.py:229`).
- Plain-speak turns on the bundled third-party Caveman skill at its default intensity for visible prose (`src/kaizen/services/plain_speak_directive.py:24`). Its activation text tells the model that the skill must not change tool use, citations or approvals (`src/kaizen/services/plain_speak_directive.py:32`), and that a toggle change applies from the next turn (`src/kaizen/services/plain_speak_directive.py:30`); these are instructions to the model, not separately enforced. The skill is pinned to an upstream commit and MIT-licensed (`src/kaizen/skills/caveman/PROVENANCE.md:5`, `src/kaizen/skills/caveman/PROVENANCE.md:9`).
- Prompt trim removes listed filler from the copy of a message sent to the model; the transcript keeps the member's own words (`src/kaizen/services/prompt_fluff_stripper.py:4`). Unusual hedging survives because the rule list is fixed (`src/kaizen/services/prompt_fluff_stripper.py:8`).

No savings figure is guaranteed. Token savings are reported as estimates (`src/kaizen/member/routes/compression.py:127`), and Plain-speak's eligible size is itself estimated (`src/kaizen/member/routes/compression.py:123`). The 65% figure in the bundled skill text is the upstream author's claim (`src/kaizen/skills/caveman/SKILL.md:4`), not a Kaizen measurement. Reset clears only the member-level statistics (`src/kaizen/member/routes/compression.py:340`). Conversation statistics appear only for conversations the member can read (`src/kaizen/member/routes/compression.py:279`).

Manual compaction does not depend on the compression flag. It lives on the conversation routes, which are mounted without it (`src/kaizen/member/app.py:238`), and it is owner-only: shared readers and other members get not found (`src/kaizen/member/manual_compaction.py:56`). It runs in the background and streams progress events (`src/kaizen/member/routes/conversations.py:341`).

In the web app, Settings > Compression holds the switches (`web/kaizen/src/routes.tsx:126`), and chat offers a "Compact this chat" command, `/compact` (`web/kaizen/src/lib/commands.ts:68`, `web/kaizen/src/lib/manualCompactionCommand.ts:1`), which starts a compaction (`web/kaizen/src/screens/chat/use-manual-compaction-command.tsx:170`).

capabilities.title: Stream Kaizen conversation events
capabilities.summary:
- open a conversation's event stream (`GET /api/conversations/{conversation_id}/events`, SDK `ConversationService.stream_events_canonical`)
- replay events after a journal position (`after` query parameter; the server also accepts a `Last-Event-ID` header)
- send a message and wait for this turn's reply over the stream (SDK `ConversationService.chat_canonical`)
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
On by default in Kaizen 0.6.0. The event route is registered with no route flag and the member API that carries it is mounted under `/api` while `MEMBER_API_ENABLED` is true, which is its default. In the SDK these methods live on `client.conversations` and take the Kaizen instance's `base_url` and an optional workroom ID.

The caller must be a Kaizen member. Access is resolved each time a stream is opened, and a conversation the member cannot access answers `not_found`. A cursor the journal rejects answers `collaboration_conflict` ("replay requires resync"). If a request sends both `after` and `Last-Event-ID`, they must match.

`stream_events_canonical` returns the raw streamed response. The caller parses the event frames and closes the response, and the method does not reconnect. Its socket read timeout defaults to 30 seconds. `chat_canonical` submits the message through the conversation's `/inputs` route and then reads the stream from the accepted position. It reopens the stream from the last position it saw when opening the stream raises `APIError` (`kamiwaza_sdk/services/kaizen.py:1086`) or the stream closes before the turn ends (`kamiwaza_sdk/services/kaizen.py:1150`), until its wait budget runs out (default 60 seconds). It then raises `ConversationError` if its last attempt to open the stream failed, and `TimeoutError` otherwise. An error while reading an open stream is not retried and raises `ConversationError` (`kamiwaza_sdk/services/kaizen.py:301`): at once for a broken connection, or when the socket read timeout, set to the remaining budget (`kamiwaza_sdk/services/kaizen.py:1084`), expires on a stream that has gone silent. It also raises `ConversationError` if the run ends in failure. Other errors while opening, such as `AuthenticationError`, are not `APIError` subclasses (`kamiwaza_sdk/exceptions.py:103`) and are raised at once. Passing no budget submits the message and returns without reading the stream.

This document makes no claim about how long past events stay available for replay.

Kaizen Legacy 2.0.4 (catalog identity `kaizen-legacy`) does not use this contract. Its events route returns paginated JSON (offset and limit), and the SDK reads it with `get_events`. The existing `kaizen.data-chat` document says the SDK has no streaming; that is out of date for the SDK at this revision and is unchanged by this batch.

capabilities.summary:
- open in canvas
- export as md, docx or pdf

conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
On by default in the packaged install. The whole upload surface, including the canvas and export routes, is mounted only when DOCUMENT_IMPORT_ENABLED is true (src/kaizen/member/app.py:348). The packaged install sets it to true (kamiwaza.json:130); the bare Settings default is false (src/kaizen/config.py:2047). Export and download also need DOCUMENT_EXPORT_ENABLED, which defaults to true (src/kaizen/config.py:2117, kamiwaza.json:131) and is a live flag in Kaizen Admin (src/kaizen/admin/catalog.py:332). With it off, the export routes return 404 (src/kaizen/member/routes/uploads.py:1292) while opening and editing keep working.

Owner only. Every canvas and export route resolves the document for the signed-in owner and returns 404 for anyone else (src/kaizen/member/routes/uploads.py:388). Only processed, text-extractable documents open in the canvas, so images do not (src/kaizen/member/routes/uploads.py:1200). Opening again returns the existing canvas (src/kaizen/member/routes/uploads.py:1203). A save appends a new version rather than overwriting (src/kaizen/member/routes/artifacts.py:353). Export uses the latest canvas version, or the extracted text if the canvas was never opened (src/kaizen/member/routes/uploads.py:1247). Exports are stored under the document and are removed with it (src/kaizen/member/routes/uploads.py:1280).

Export formats are exactly md, docx and pdf; there is no other export format. PDF layout is best-effort (src/kaizen/services/document_export.py:12). Images are embedded only from the member's own content. A remote, missing or unreadable image renders as its alt text, and export never fetches an image URL: remote and `data:` image targets are dropped before any lookup (src/kaizen/services/document_export.py:83, src/kaizen/services/export_images.py:89).

UI reach. Members open the canvas from the Documents screen (web/kaizen/src/screens/Documents.tsx:578) and save edits in the artifact panel (web/kaizen/src/components/ArtifactPanel.tsx:1358). The web client defines a function for the export route (web/kaizen/src/lib/api/endpoints.ts:854), but no screen calls it at this revision. DOCX and PDF export is established as API only.

capabilities.title: Daily model-token budget per member
capabilities.summary:
- set the per-member daily cap (through the settings update route, which `kaizen.admin-settings-console` declares)
- check a member's usage before a direct model call
- refuse the call once the cap is reached
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
On by default, with a cap of 10,000,000 tokens per member per day (src/kaizen/config.py:330, kamiwaza.json:135). The install manifest lists it as "Daily model-token budget per member" (kamiwaza.json:593). Kaizen admins can change it as a live setting in the Rate limits group of the admin Settings screen (src/kaizen/admin/catalog.py:581, web/kaizen/src/routes.tsx:157). The settings routes require a Kaizen admin (src/kaizen/member/routes/ops.py:37). A setting is editable only when the config store is on (src/kaizen/admin/service.py:193). The packaged install turns the config store on (kamiwaza.json:172); the bare Settings default is off (src/kaizen/config.py:1663).

Usage is the sum of prompt and response tokens on successful calls in Kaizen's LLM audit ledger since the start of the current UTC day (src/kaizen/repositories/llm_audit.py:59). The check compares usage already recorded with the cap before the call runs (src/kaizen/llm_gateway/policy.py:92). It does not reserve the cost of the call about to run, so one call can take a member past the cap. Embedding calls made by Kaizen's system requester, which it uses for connector and uploaded-document ingestion, skip the check (src/kaizen/llm_gateway/policy.py:86).

The check runs on Kaizen's direct model gateway (src/kaizen/llm_gateway/factory.py:134, src/kaizen/llm_gateway/client.py:357) and on the model proxy used by the agent runtime, which answers an over-cap request with HTTP 429 `budget_exceeded` (src/kaizen/member/routes/pi_model_proxy.py:309). The setting's source comment says over-cap calls fail closed with `BudgetExceeded` and use the existing fallback path (src/kaizen/config.py:328); that fallback was not traced for this document. This document does not establish that every model call in Kaizen passes through these two paths.

The cap counts tokens, per member, per UTC day. It is not a currency spending cap and not a total across all members. It is separate from the platform's delegated-model caps (delegation.brokered-resource-access) and from the platform's activity records (platform.usage-and-audit).

capabilities.title: Prebuilt specialist agents
capabilities.summary:
- provision the bundled agents at startup
- list them in the Agents gallery
- choose one for a chat turn
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
On by default. At startup Kaizen provisions every bundle in its agent-bundle directory unless AGENT_BUNDLES_ENABLED is false (src/kaizen/agents/bundles.py:533, src/kaizen/config.py:2014). The image copies the four bundles into that directory (docker/Dockerfile:143), and the service runs the loader before it starts serving (src/kaizen/main.py:322). Loading is best-effort: a bundle that fails is logged and skipped, and startup continues (src/kaizen/agents/bundles.py:543). If an agent with the same name already exists and the bundle did not create it, the bundle leaves it alone and does not add its own (src/kaizen/agents/bundles.py:433).

Bundle agents are created shared and protected (src/kaizen/agents/bundles.py:482, src/kaizen/agents/bundles.py:490). A shared agent is published to all members with use access (src/kaizen/repositories/studio.py:940, src/kaizen/repositories/studio.py:1105). Members see them in the Agents gallery (web/kaizen/src/screens/Agents.tsx:590), which needs MEMBER_AGENTS_ENABLED (src/kaizen/member/routes/agents.py:611), default true (src/kaizen/config.py:1923). A chat request picks an agent by `agent_id` (src/kaizen/member/schemas.py:322). Each of the four bundles marks its agent routable (for example agent_bundles/web-researcher/bundle.yaml:27), so the agents can also be candidates for automatic routing; that routing is a separate capability.

The roster is the set of bundle directories, not a Python list, so the declaration is open. At this revision the directories are Web Researcher (agent_bundles/web-researcher/bundle.yaml:20), Software Engineer (agent_bundles/software-engineer/bundle.yaml:13), Ontology Builder (agent_bundles/ontology-builder/bundle.yaml:9) and Demo Builder (agent_bundles/demo-builder/bundle.yaml:8).

- Web Researcher searches and reads the public web through its pi-web-access package (agent_bundles/web-researcher/bundle.yaml:10). Inferred from that description, not tested: it needs outbound internet access to be useful.
- Ontology Builder produces a Kaizen graph artifact and is told not to create or query a Graphiti instance (agent_bundles/ontology-builder/bundle.yaml:32). It is not persistent graph memory.
- Demo Builder is described as a staff workflow for Kamiwaza and Kaizen demos (agent_bundles/demo-builder/bundle.yaml:20). Its package README says it reconciles live demo resources through Kaizen's `inspect_kamiwaza` and `manage_kamiwaza_demo` tools (agent_bundles/demo-builder/packages/@kaizen__demo-builder@1.0.0/README.md:13).

Shipping an agent does not establish that its model output is correct or useful.

capabilities.title: Warn about or redact sensitive text before a chat message is sent
capabilities.summary:
- set a conversation's Privacy Guard mode: off, warn or redact
- set an agent's default mode in the agent wizard
- read a conversation's effective mode
- scan message text before send
- warn: review the findings, then send redacted, send as typed or keep editing
- redact: replace each finding with `<REDACTED>` and send
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
This is Kaizen Legacy 2.0.4 (`kamiwaza-extensions-kaizen`), not the primary Kaizen 0.6.0. In Kaizen 0.6.0 the LLM gateway states that Kaizen does not apply a redaction policy to model input (`src/kaizen/llm_gateway/policy.py:104` in `kamiwaza-extensions-tomo`).

Privacy Guard is off by default. When neither the conversation nor its agent sets a valid mode, the effective mode is `off` (`backend/app/api/v1/conversations.py:2166`). A conversation override wins. Otherwise the agent's `agent_context.privacy_filter` mode applies (`backend/app/api/v1/conversations.py:2157`), which the agent wizard writes when the chosen mode is not off (`frontend/app/components/agent-creation-wizard.tsx:608`). The backend accepts only `off`, `warn` and `redact` (`backend/app/api/v1/conversations.py:1989`, `backend/app/api/v1/conversations.py:2020`). While a conversation's settings are loading, or if they fail to load, the chat page uses warn mode (`frontend/app/conversations/[id]/page.tsx:486`, `frontend/app/conversations/[id]/page.tsx:488`).

The check runs in the browser, in the message box's send handler (`frontend/app/components/chat/message-input.tsx:106`). The settings panel calls it a light browser-side review (`frontend/app/components/chat/conversation-settings-panel.tsx:525`). The backend stores and returns the mode, and a search of the backend Python at this revision found no code that applies it to message text. So a client that calls the message API directly is not checked; that is inferred from where the check lives, not run.

Detection is a fixed list of regular expressions (`frontend/lib/privacy-guard.ts:29`): email addresses, US-style phone numbers, SSNs written as `123-45-6789`, IPv4 addresses, `sk-` keys and several key, token, secret and password patterns (`frontend/lib/privacy-guard.ts:49`). It is not data-loss prevention and will miss identifiers outside those patterns. Only the typed text is scanned; attached images are sent unchanged (`frontend/app/components/chat/message-input.tsx:115`). In warn mode the user can still send the original text (`frontend/app/components/chat/message-input.tsx:370`).

The settings routes are `GET` and `PATCH /api/conversations/{conversation_id}/settings` (`backend/app/main.py:210`, `backend/app/api/v1/conversations.py:1918`, `backend/app/api/v1/conversations.py:2735`). Changing a conversation's mode requires ownership of the conversation (`backend/app/api/v1/conversations.py:2806`) and, in a shared workroom, a write-capable role: owner, editor, contributor or member (`backend/app/utils/workroom_access.py:34`, checked at `backend/app/api/v1/conversations.py:2787`).

The privacy-mode registry is a closed declaration. The route table is open: this document establishes the named positive operations, not an exhaustive unsupported-feature list.

capabilities.title: Save tool calls as recipes that agents can look up
capabilities.summary:
- save a tool call from search results as a recipe
- list recipes
- view a recipe's arguments and result
- rename a recipe or edit its notes
- delete a recipe
- look up recipes from an agent by tool name or keyword
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
This is Kaizen Legacy 2.0.4 (`kamiwaza-extensions-kaizen`), not the primary Kaizen 0.6.0.

Recipes are on by default, with no feature flag. The recipe routes are mounted under `/api/recipes` (`backend/app/main.py:231`, `backend/app/api/v1/recipes.py:34`). The lookup tool is added to every OpenHands agent when a conversation is created (`backend/app/services/conversation_manager.py:1434`) and when it resumes (`backend/app/services/conversation_manager.py:2892`), and a per-conversation tool selection keeps it (`backend/app/services/conversation_manager.py:1148`). In the UI, recipes live on the Search page (`frontend/app/components/navigation.tsx:21`). A tool-call result has a Save as Recipe button (`frontend/app/search/page.tsx:641`), only tool-call events can be saved (`frontend/app/search/page.tsx:184`), and the Recipes tab lists what was saved (`frontend/app/search/page.tsx:712`).

Saving replaces sensitive values with `[REDACTED]` (`backend/app/utils/recipe_payload.py:9`). That covers values under keys such as password, secret, token, API key, authorization, cookie and private key (`backend/app/utils/recipe_payload.py:13`), and strings that look like bearer tokens, `sk-` or `rk-` keys, AWS access keys or JWTs (`backend/app/utils/recipe_payload.py:24`). The arguments and the result are each capped at 128 KB (`backend/app/utils/recipe_payload.py:10`), and a larger payload gets HTTP 413 (`backend/app/api/v1/recipes.py:54`). After saving, only the name and notes can change (`backend/app/api/v1/recipes.py:154`, `backend/app/schemas/recipe.py:18`).

Visibility follows the workroom. In a shared workroom every member sees the workroom's recipes; in the Global workroom each user sees only their own (`backend/app/utils/resource_scope.py:41`, `backend/app/utils/resource_scope.py:42`). Rename and delete use the same filter, so in a shared workroom any member with a write-capable role (owner, editor, contributor or member) can change or remove another member's recipe (`backend/app/api/v1/recipes.py:188`, `backend/app/utils/workroom_access.py:34`).

The agent lookup needs a tool name or a keyword (`backend/app/api/v1/agent_context.py:1441`). The keyword matches recipe names, notes and arguments (`backend/app/api/v1/agent_context.py:1469`). It searches within the conversation's user and workroom (`backend/app/api/v1/agent_context.py:1457`) and returns at most the 20 newest matches (`backend/app/api/v1/agent_context.py:1473`). The text the agent reads cuts arguments and results at 500 characters each (`backend/agent_tools/recipe_lookup/schemas.py:63`). A recipe returns the stored arguments and result as saved (`backend/app/api/v1/agent_context.py:1483`, `backend/app/api/v1/agent_context.py:1484`). Nothing re-runs or checks them, so a recipe does not show that the call still works.

capabilities.title: Typing indicators in shared chats
capabilities.summary:
- join chat presence by opening the live event stream
- set or clear typing
- leave chat presence
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
On by default wherever a chat has been shared. The event, typing and presence routes are mounted without a flag of their own (src/kaizen/member/app.py:240). Other members reach a chat through shared-chat invitations (src/kaizen/member/routes/collaboration.py:176) or through project access. The invitation routes are request-gated by SHARED_CHAT_COLLABORATION_ENABLED (src/kaizen/member/app.py:487), and project access also requires that flag (src/kaizen/services/project_workspace_features.py:14). It defaults to true (src/kaizen/config.py:1770).

Setting typing needs write access to the conversation (src/kaizen/member/conversation_live.py:293). Opening the event stream opens a presence lease, keyed to the tab's connection id when the client sends one (src/kaizen/member/routes/collaboration_runtime.py:226, src/kaizen/member/conversation_live.py:422). Leaving removes only that tab's lease (src/kaizen/member/conversation_live.py:508). A member never sees their own typing, and only members with a live presence lease are shown as typing (src/kaizen/member/conversation_presence.py:67, src/kaizen/member/conversation_presence.py:69). The web client sends typing only in a collaborative room (web/kaizen/src/screens/Chat.tsx:982) and shows "... is typing" in the chat (web/kaizen/src/screens/chat/participant-strip.tsx:150, web/kaizen/src/screens/Chat.tsx:2502).

State is ephemeral and kept in Valkey (src/kaizen/member/conversation_presence.py:1, src/kaizen/config.py:1845). Leases are short-lived: the presence TTL is at most 30 seconds (src/kaizen/config.py:1834) and the typing TTL at most 10 seconds (src/kaizen/member/conversation_live.py:193). If the store is unavailable, presence reports itself unavailable with no typing members (src/kaizen/member/conversation_live.py:608), and the indicator is hidden (web/kaizen/src/screens/chat/participant-strip.tsx:157).

This is Kaizen's own chat-scoped presence. It is not platform workroom presence (workrooms.presence), which lists teammate typing indicators as not supported.

capabilities.title: Workroom notes and in-pane text editing
capabilities.summary:
- create a note from the workroom Files panel
- create a note from the chat agent
- list workroom files and notes
- open a file's details and download link
- edit a text file's content
- rename a note and edit its content
- delete a file
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
This is Kaizen Legacy 2.0.4 (`kamiwaza-extensions-kaizen`), not the primary Kaizen 0.6.0.

The backend side is on by default. The `create_note` tool is added to every OpenHands agent when a conversation is created (`backend/app/services/conversation_manager.py:1451`) and when it resumes (`backend/app/services/conversation_manager.py:2909`). The file routes are mounted under `/api/v1/context/storage/raw` (`backend/app/main.py:227`, `backend/app/context/api.py:183`).

The in-pane editor and the New note button sit behind the frontend flag `NEXT_PUBLIC_FLAG_METADATA_EXPLORER`. The flag reads as off when unset (`frontend/lib/feature-flags.ts:18`). The frontend image build defaults it to `true` (`frontend/Dockerfile:62`), and the App Garden manifest sets it to `"true"` (`kamiwaza.json:44`) even though the manifest's own description calls it default-off (`kamiwaza.json:203`). With the flag off, the conversation page shows the older files panel (`frontend/app/components/workroom-panels/workroom-shell-slot.tsx:313`). That panel has no editor, so New note does not appear (`frontend/app/components/chat/workroom-files-panel.tsx:64`).

Notes are Markdown files under `kaizen-notes/` ending in `.md` (`backend/app/context/api.py:4419`, `backend/app/context/api.py:4420`). The agent route builds the file name from a slug of the title (`backend/app/api/v1/agent_context.py:2031`). Creating a note whose file name already exists is rejected (`backend/app/api/v1/agent_context.py:2167`, `backend/app/context/api.py:4503`). Only notes can be renamed (`backend/app/context/api.py:4438`).

Editing is limited to text types. The default allowlist is `text/*`, JSON, YAML and TOML (`backend/app/core/config.py:167`), and other types stored in Kaizen's local store get HTTP 415 (`backend/app/context/api.py:4618`); edits to platform files are forwarded without that check (`backend/app/context/api.py:4644`), and the platform's Context Service applies its own allowlist, by default only Markdown and plain text (`kamiwaza/services/context/config.py:168`, `kamiwaza/services/context/services/object_storage_service.py:913`). A content edit is capped at 65,535 bytes of UTF-8 (`backend/app/context/schemas.py:1214`, `backend/app/context/schemas.py:1245`) and must not be blank (`backend/app/context/schemas.py:1253`). An agent note body is capped at 87,380 base64 characters, about 64 KB (`backend/app/api/v1/agent_context.py:2001`).

Writes need a write-capable workroom role: owner, editor, contributor or member (`backend/app/utils/workroom_access.py:34`, checked at `backend/app/context/api.py:4602` and `backend/app/context/api.py:4669`). The UI hides New note and the edit controls from other roles (`frontend/lib/file-editor/role-gate.ts:16`). In the Global workroom, Kaizen keeps each user's files in a separate folder (`backend/app/services/workroom_raw_store.py:79`).

Kaizen stores notes and inline files on its own volume, `/app/storage/workroom_raw_files` by default (`backend/app/services/workroom_raw_store.py:35`). The file list merges these local files with the platform's (`backend/app/context/api.py:4571`). An edit to a file that is not in the local store is forwarded to the platform Context Service (`backend/app/context/api.py:4644`), which applies its own rules. That forwarding is a proxy, not a second storage engine. In the Global workroom such an edit returns 404 (`backend/app/context/api.py:4639`).

capabilities.title: Control model placement across hardware classes, including fractional GPU serving
capabilities.summary:
- estimate-model-vram
- place-deployment
- reserve-memory-budget
- classify-hardware
- serve-fractionally
- disable-fractional-sharing
- report-no-fit
- inspect-placement
conditions: The cluster exposes accelerator nodes with the labels placement classifies from, and the serving stack is installed.
limits:
- On managed clusters, placement respects whatever GPU sharing the cluster admin configured through the GPU Operator (MIG partitions, time-slicing, MPS) and requires no privileged access beyond the one-time install steps (a CRD and a read-only role for node labels). Without a configured sharing strategy, deployments still work but density is limited to one model per GPU.
- On hardware-isolated cards, capacity is the partition size, not the card: a model larger than the largest configured partition fails with a structured no-fit error even when the card as a whole is big enough.
- macOS installs run the control plane in a VM while model processes run natively on the host for Metal GPU access; they appear as standalone topology with the `metal_spawner` sharing class.
- The `surface` front matter above declares UI and API, while the estimator guarantee names the SDK method `client.serving.estimate_model_vram()`. The declared value is reproduced verbatim from the 2026-08-09 inventory run and is left as recorded rather than corrected here, so a consumer reading `surface` should not infer that the SDK estimator is unavailable. Reconciling the declaration is a change for the inventory's next pass.

capabilities.title: Serve models on an SSH-paired second GPU node
capabilities.summary:
- attach a paired node (`POST /cluster/attach_pairing`)
- detach the paired node (`POST /cluster/detach_pairing`)
- start model containers on the paired node (vLLM two-node Ray worker, llama.cpp)
- sync downloaded model files to the paired node
- report the paired node and its GPU inventory in cluster capabilities
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
Off until an administrator attaches a node. There is no separate feature flag: the settings are disabled when no remote host is stored (`kamiwaza/serving/two_node.py:190`), and the dataclass default is `enabled: bool = False` (`kamiwaza/serving/two_node.py:96`). The attach and detach routes are on the cluster router, which every install mounts (`kamiwaza/app.py:738`). Both routes require the admin role (`kamiwaza/cluster/api.py:64`). Setting `KAMIWAZA_PAIRED_NODE` in the API environment also attaches a node, after the same SSH check, when the settings first load (`kamiwaza/serving/two_node.py:156`).

Attach checks that the node answers over SSH before it saves anything (`kamiwaza/serving/two_node.py:223`). Only one paired node is supported; a second attach is refused (`kamiwaza/cluster/nodes.py:438`). SSH host-key checking is off unless the caller sets `strict_host_key_checking` (`kamiwaza/cluster/schemas/cluster.py:661`). vLLM starts a container on the paired node only when the launch targets it. `auto` stays local (`kamiwaza/serving/engines/VLLMEngine.py:3780`), and the two-node Ray launch puts the worker there by default (`kamiwaza/serving/two_node_launcher.py:372`). llama.cpp starts every container on the paired node while one is attached (`kamiwaza/serving/engines/LlamaCppEngine.py:1744`).

The path is Docker over SSH in the vLLM and llama.cpp engines. The Kubernetes engine adapters do not call the two-node runner at this revision, so support on a Kubernetes install is not established. The two-node guide was retired, and `platform.kubernetes-install` lists a published two-node topology as not supported. This document records only that the source ships the admin API and the serving path. It is not evidence of other multi-node layouts or of every GPU vendor.

capabilities.title: Retire every workroom in an organization under a confirmed plan
capabilities.summary:
- list the organization's room inventory
- create a decommission plan (strategy, cutoff, retention contact)
- confirm a plan with the organization name
- delete the planned rooms at the cutoff (background task)
- read a room's tombstone
- read and update organization room settings (organization name, room creation policy)
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
Administrator API, with one exception: reading a room's tombstone is open to any signed-in member of the tenant. The routes are on `room_control_router`, which the console router includes (`kamiwaza/services/console/api.py:46`) and every install mounts (`kamiwaza/app.py:841`). Every route except the tombstone read requires the admin role (`kamiwaza/services/console/room_api.py:23`). No decommission happens until an administrator creates a plan: an organization with no settings row reports `decommission_state` `none` and `creation_policy` `anyone` (`kamiwaza/services/console/room_controls.py:376`). Plans are scoped to the caller's tenant. The room creation policy in the settings is `anyone`, `admins` or `off` (`kamiwaza/services/console/room_schemas.py:14`): `admins` limits room creation to administrators, and `off` refuses it to everyone (`kamiwaza/services/console/room_policy.py:10`, `kamiwaza/services/console/room_policy.py:12`).

Creating a plan needs a future, timezone-aware cutoff (`kamiwaza/services/console/room_controls.py:486`) and turns room creation off at once (`kamiwaza/services/console/room_controls.py:500`). It stays off while the plan waits for confirmation: the settings update refuses any other creation policy while a draft plan exists (`kamiwaza/services/console/room_controls.py:451`), and the room-control routes have no way to cancel a plan. The earlier policy comes back only when a confirmation with the correct organization name finds that the cutoff has passed, before or during the confirmation, and discards the expired draft (`kamiwaza/services/console/room_controls.py:538`, `kamiwaza/services/console/room_controls.py:558`, `kamiwaza/services/console/room_controls.py:574`, `kamiwaza/services/console/room_controls.py:598`). Confirmation needs `confirm: true` (`kamiwaza/services/console/room_schemas.py:68`) and the exact organization name from the settings (`kamiwaza/services/console/room_controls.py:539`). It fails if the room inventory changed after the plan was created (`kamiwaza/services/console/room_controls.py:549`). That failure leaves the draft in place, and no new plan can be created while a draft exists (`kamiwaza/services/console/room_controls.py:495`): the draft can be confirmed only once the inventory matches it again, or is discarded by a correctly named confirmation after its cutoff. Room creation stays off meanwhile. While a plan is active, workroom changes return 409 (`kamiwaza/services/workrooms/api.py:706`) and room creation is refused (`kamiwaza/services/console/room_policy.py:11`). A background task started with the API looks for plans past their cutoff every 30 seconds (`kamiwaza/services/console/room_controls.py:722`). At the cutoff each room is marked deleted (`kamiwaza/services/console/room_controls.py:179`), then its access relations are cleaned up and its resources scheduled for purge.

The two strategy values, `retain_then_delete` and `delete`, behave the same at this revision: rooms are archived at confirmation and deleted at the cutoff (`kamiwaza/services/console/room_schemas.py:44`). Export planning is not offered and legal-hold counts are not available (`kamiwaza/services/console/room_schemas.py:37`). Any signed-in user in the tenant can read a tombstone. Its state is `read_only` before the cutoff and `tombstone` after. The global workroom is left out of the inventory.

API only. The ui-v2 decommission page is not built into an image at this revision; the frontend image target builds `./frontend` (`docker-bake.hcl:367`), which has no decommission page. This is separate from `workrooms.archive-and-delete` (one room at a time) and `workrooms.admin-oversight` (list and delete).

capabilities.title: Per-tool OAuth operation policies
capabilities.summary:
- create a tool policy (`POST /oauth-broker/policies/`)
- read a tool policy by ID (`GET /oauth-broker/policies/{policy_id}`)
- list tool policies, optionally filtered by app or tool (`GET /oauth-broker/policies/`)
- update a policy's allowed operations, allowed scope subset or metadata (`PATCH /oauth-broker/policies/{policy_id}`)
- delete a tool policy (`DELETE /oauth-broker/policies/{policy_id}`)
- enforce the allowed operations before a call on the broker's standard proxy path (and at legacy ephemeral token minting), answering 403 on a violation
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
On by default, API only. The OAuth broker router is mounted with no feature flag, and the policy routes sit under it at `/oauth-broker/policies`. No SDK method calls these routes. The UI source holds only generated API types for them; no shipped UI screen was found.

Creating, reading, changing or deleting a policy requires the caller to own its app installation or to be an administrator; anyone else gets 403, and an unknown policy id gets 404 before that check. A list request without an app filter returns every policy to an administrator and only the policies of the caller's own app installations to anyone else.

Enforcement denies by default. A proxied call is refused unless the tool is in the app installation's `allowed_tools`, a policy exists for that app, tool and provider, and the requested operation is in the policy's `allowed_operations`. A tool with no policy for a provider cannot make any call to that provider through the standard proxy.

The check runs on the broker's standard proxy path (`/oauth-broker/proxy/{provider}/{service}/{operation}`) and on legacy ephemeral token minting, where it is checked as the operation `token.mint`. The delegated-workload execution path does not call it; that path authorizes each call with a one-use lease instead. Policies govern those two broker paths only, not tool execution in general. The broker's connector routes (`POST /oauth-broker/connectors/{connector_id}/proxy` and `/identity-proxy`, and `POST /oauth-broker/tokens/connectors/{connector_id}/mint`) do not check tool policies (`kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/api/connector_proxy.py:34`, `kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/api/connector_proxy.py:38`, `kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/api/tokens.py:37`, `kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/api/tokens.py:152`). All three require the caller to be the connector's bound workload (`kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/connector_token_service.py:245`). The two proxy routes also enforce the connector's egress allowlist (`kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/connector_proxy_service.py:68`, `kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/connector_proxy_service.py:109`). The mint route has no egress check: it checks the requested scopes against the granted ones and returns the provider token to the connector (`kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/connector_token_service.py:177`, `kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/connector_token_service.py:114`). For a per-user connection that token is the connection's own provider token, not narrowed to the requested scopes; the scopes are recorded on the lease and returned as `granted_scopes` (`kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/connector_token_service.py:178`, `kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/connector_token_service.py:101`, `kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/connector_token_service.py:116`).

Operation names come from the broker's registered operation list. At this revision only Google operations are registered: Gmail (`gmail.search`, `gmail.getMessage`, `gmail.send`, `gmail.listLabels`, `gmail.modify`), Drive (`drive.listFiles`, `drive.getFile`) and Calendar (`calendar.list`, `calendar.events`). The create route stores the submitted operation names without checking them against that list.

A read-only Gmail tool is possible: a policy that lists `gmail.search` and `gmail.getMessage` but not `gmail.send` refuses sends. The email tool deployment does not start that way. When the tool service provisions OAuth for an email tool, it creates a policy for `email-mcp` that allows `gmail.send` and `gmail.modify`. An owner must update that policy to make the tool read-only.

`allowed_scope_subset` is checked only when a legacy ephemeral token is minted, and an empty list places no limit there. The proxy path does not check it.

capabilities.title: Tell the two Kaizen products apart under a shared catalog name
capabilities.summary:
- classify a release under a shared Kaizen name as the v3 or the v4 product line
- identify Kaizen v4 from product-owned compose markers

conditions: A catalog-sourced extension release carrying compose content.
limits:
**The product line is derived from compose content, never from version order.** The two products keep unrelated version lines, so a version comparison gets this wrong: Kaizen v3 ships as `kaizen-legacy` at a *v2* version carrying v3 compose. Classification returns nothing when the question does not apply: the name is not one the two products share, or there is no compose to classify. An absent answer is not a negative one.

Trust requires all three of a reserved name, a `kamiwaza` catalog source, and no overlay shadow; a shadowed row fails closed, because the catalog-overlay endpoint is open to any authenticated user. **Nothing is blocked on an untrusted verdict** — what is withheld is canonical presentation, not the action. `kz-ext dev` shadows a reserved name in the ordinary course of development and keeps working.

`kaizen-next` is retired as a product label and is retained only so stale catalog rows under it still resolve.

capabilities.title: Deploy curated applications from the App Garden
capabilities.summary:
- Browse the App Garden catalog and refresh available releases from the remote catalog; refreshing does not select a release or create a local template.
- Deploy an app from a template, by template id or by name (optionally version-pinned), with environment variables and scaling parameters, into the caller's workroom.
- Check whether a template's container images are pulled, and pull them ahead of a first deploy.
- List and read deployments, read a deployment's status and instances, and stop or purge a deployment.
- Deploy with platform-supplied OpenAI-compatible and routing environment variables and routing-aware template variables, with reserved keys in user input dropped.
- Mark a deployment ephemeral so it is purged on logout or session expiry.
conditions: The App Garden catalog is populated — either the remote catalog is enabled and synced, or garden apps have been imported as templates.
For apps that use AI features, at least one model deployment is healthy; App Garden injects OpenAI-compatible environment variables automatically.
limits:
- **The Docker-Compose App Garden surface is deprecated in favor of Kubernetes CRD-based extensions.** The platform's `deploy_app` endpoint returns RFC 8594 `Deprecation`/`Warning` headers directing callers to `POST /extensions`, and the SDK's `AppService` emits a `DeprecationWarning` recommending `ExtensionService`. The verbs documented above function today — and `install_by_name` is explicitly the current install-by-name path — but new integrations should expect the extensions API to be the successor surface. This document claims the App Garden surface as it stands, not its successor.
- Deploying requires an authenticated user; catalog administration (choosing and refreshing the approved remote catalog source) is an administrator concern.
- Apps run with the configuration their template defines; most work with defaults, and model-preference settings must be chosen before deploying where an app exposes them.

- **The bundled catalog is not the whole catalog.** The catalog packaged in the chart lists seven apps at the cited deploy revision (`hello-web`, `connector-builder`, `skills-library`, `service-graphiti`, `service-milvus`, `kaizen`, `kaizen-legacy`). `service-vespa` and `workroom-manager` were in it at the revision this document first cited and are no longer; their absence from the bundled file says nothing about the remote catalog.
- **What was re-read.** The catalog, route, reserved-key and SDK citations in front matter were re-read at the revisions in `source_scope`. The teardown fence, the ephemeral purge and the routing-aware template variables were confirmed present by symbol at those revisions and were not re-traced end to end.

capabilities.title: Verify and retain the shipped app baseline a deployment was built from
capabilities.summary:
- load the shipped baseline from its configured path
- verify the file against its expected SHA256 **before** parsing it
- validate the baseline's structure and reject a malformed one
- retain exactly one release per name as an immutable baseline member
- refuse a baseline member incompatible with the running Core version
conditions: KAMIWAZA_EXTENSION_BASELINE_PATH and KAMIWAZA_EXTENSION_BASELINE_SHA256 must both be set; the baseline file must be readable by Core.
limits:
**The digest is checked before the content is parsed**, and a missing or non-64-hex expected digest is itself a refusal — an unverified baseline is not loaded at all rather than loaded and flagged.

Compatibility is decided **per row**, by that row's own recorded Core version and canonical core line. A row without one is compatible with any Core. **Any `core_version` recorded in the baseline itself is ignored** — the running Core decides, not the file.

**One incompatible member refuses the whole baseline.** There is no partial retention: the baseline is an all-or-nothing identity, which is also why the digest-pin requirement below deliberately exempts it.

Two releases under the same name in one baseline is a refusal, not a last-one-wins merge.

This covers the baseline a deployment was *built from*. It is not a change history of what was deployed over time, and nothing here reverts a deployment.

capabilities.title: Require digest-pinned images on newly published app releases
capabilities.summary:
- report whether the digest-pin requirement is enabled for this deployment
- refuse a newly published release whose artifacts are not digest-pinned
- surface that refusal as a distinct, catchable condition rather than a generic validation error
conditions: Off unless KAMIWAZA_EXTENSION_REQUIRE_DIGEST_PINS is set to a recognized true value.
limits:
**Off by default.** This is an operator opt-in, enabled by environment configuration; an unrecognized value is reported rather than silently treated as enabled.

The requirement applies **only** to releases of `published` provenance that are **not yet retained**. A release already retained keeps its identity, so a publisher can still withdraw it — tightening the rule must not strand what is already in use.

Canonical rows are validated strictly on **every** path regardless of this setting; the setting does not relax them.

**The shipped baseline is never held to this rule.** It is identified by its packaged SHA256, and because one refused member would refuse the whole baseline, applying a pin requirement to it would turn an operator preference into an install failure. See `apps.deployment-baseline`.

**This is pinning, not rollback.** It constrains how a new release may be published; it does not revert a deployment to a previous release, and nothing here establishes rollback within or across product generations.

capabilities.title: Select the workload backend for an extension's code sandbox
capabilities.summary:
- select the sandbox workload provider per extension
- run a warm pool of sandbox workers, with a declared update strategy for template changes
- bound a claim's lifetime so claims left behind by a crashed controller are reclaimed
- constrain sandbox worker images to an allowlist
- mirror the sandbox worker token (`SANDBOX_WORKER_TOKEN`), supplied inline or from the extension's own operator-owned Secret, into a deployment-scoped Secret in the sandbox namespace
conditions: The agentSandbox provider additionally requires a pinned kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox platform install supplying extensions.agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1.
limits:
**This selects a workload backend. It does not change the isolation boundary.** The default sandbox isolation posture for this release is the standard shared-kernel container runtime, and choosing the Agent Sandbox provider does not alter that. A gVisor RuntimeClass is **not** offered as an install option in 1.3.0; it is tracked separately for a later cycle. The resource does carry an optional `agentSandbox.runtimeClassName` field that names a RuntimeClass the cluster already provides; it is empty by default, and nothing here installs, selects or qualifies one. Any claim that extension code runs under a stronger-than-container boundary is unsupported here.

**Opt-in, and the default is unchanged.** Existing extensions stay on the Pod/Service/PVC backend; nothing is migrated by enabling the provider elsewhere.

**The worker token is Secret-only.** The token the operator mirrors is the sandbox *worker* token, `SANDBOX_WORKER_TOKEN`, set on the sandbox-controller service either inline or as a `secretKeyRef` to the extension's own operator-owned Opaque Secret. It is written to a `<name>-sandbox-worker-token` Secret in the sandbox namespace, and warm-pool pods reference that mirror through `secretKeyRef` and never carry the value. **A ConfigMap source, or any other non-Secret `valueFrom`, is refused at admission and again in the resolver**; a Secret that is not the extension's own is refused for lacking owner provenance. No ConfigMap-sourced token path exists and none is claimed.

**The bounds are conditional.** The claim-lifetime bound applies only when `maxLifetimeSeconds` is set: the sandbox controller then writes and renews a shutdown time on each claim, and the operator separately reaps claims older than the cap. With it unset neither applies, and a reaper failure is logged rather than returned. Acting on the shutdown time, and replacing warm sandboxes under the declared update strategy, is done by the upstream agent-sandbox controller, which is outside the sourced repositories. The image allowlist (`imageWhitelist`) is a prefix match; an empty list imposes no constraint.

The Agent Sandbox provider requires a **platform prerequisite installed beforehand**: a pinned agent-sandbox release providing the `extensions.agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1` API. **The operator deliberately does not create those CRDs dynamically**, so an install that skips the prerequisite fails rather than self-provisioning. Production and offline deployments are expected to mirror that release asset through the normal Kamiwaza supply chain rather than fetch it during reconciliation.

capabilities.title: Administer local user accounts
capabilities.summary:
- **Create an account that can sign in.** `POST /auth/users/local` (the SDK's `create_local_user`) creates the local account and provisions its Keycloak identity with the supplied password (v1.2.1 code, `_provision_and_link_keycloak`), so a password grant for that user succeeds immediately (measured). A new account defaults to the `user` role, is active, and is not deleted (measured: research probe S2 and the lifecycle test).
- **Read and list accounts.** `GET /auth/users/{id}` (`get_user`) returns the account, and `GET /auth/users/` (`list_users`) includes it (measured, lifecycle test).
- **Change account details.** `PUT /auth/users/{id}` (`update_user`) updates the account. The evidence arm changes the email and reads back the new value. It does not change `roles` or `active` as an administrator.
- **Reset a password.** `POST /auth/users/{id}/password` (`reset_user_password`) sets a new password. The new password signs in and the replaced one is rejected (measured, lifecycle test). With authentication enabled, Keycloak is authoritative for the password and the local password hash is left untouched (v1.2.1 code, `_reset_password_keycloak`; not observable through the API).
- **Refuse non-administrators.** A signed-in user without the admin role receives 403 ("Admin role required") when it lists accounts, reads its own account, updates its own account to grant itself the admin role, resets its own password, or deletes its own account. Afterwards its roles are unchanged, it is not deleted, and its original password still signs in (measured, lifecycle test). The SDK's local guard `require_admin` raises `AuthorizationError` for ForwardAuth headers that lack the admin role and passes for an administrator's (measured, lifecycle test).
- **Remove an account from administration.** `DELETE /auth/users/{id}` (`delete_user`) marks the account deleted and inactive; it then reads as 404 and no longer appears in the user list (measured, lifecycle test).
conditions: The deployment runs with authentication enabled and the platform Keycloak reachable; creating a local account provisions the Keycloak identity the account signs in with (v1.2.1 code, `_provision_and_link_keycloak`).

The caller holds the platform admin role. In v1.2.1 the routes this capability covers (create, list, read, update, password reset, and delete of accounts) require it; a user's own password-change routes under /auth/users/me do not.
limits:
- **Deletion did not revoke access on the Azure 1.2.1 deployment** (observed 2026-09-16).
  - After deletion the account could still obtain tokens with its password, and a personal access token it had created still authenticated. The SDK tests `test_deleted_local_user_cannot_sign_in` and `test_deleted_local_user_pat_stops_authenticating` pin both as strict expected failures.
  - The ENG-12326 research probe also found that the access token issued before deletion kept working.
  - The v1.2.1 platform code is consistent with this: deletion is a soft delete in the platform database that does not disable the Keycloak identity, and the platform revokes the account's PATs by its local user id while PATs are owned by its Keycloak subject id.
  - Do not describe deleting a local user as ending that user's access.
- **Refusal of account creation to a non-administrator is not established here.** In the v1.2.1 platform code the create route (`POST /auth/users/local`, `create_local`) takes the same `AdminContext` dependency as the routes above. The evidence arm does not attempt it, because an accepted create would leave another identity behind.
- **Account identifiers differ.** On that deployment the account's local id was not the `sub` its tokens carried (research probe). Code keyed on one can miss records keyed on the other, as deletion's PAT revocation does. A lookup through `GET /auth/users/resolve/{identifier}` accepts either identifier for an account that is not deleted, and answers 404 for a deleted one (v1.2.1 `resolve_user_by_identifier`, `get_user_by_identifier`).
- **Usernames are not reusable after deletion.** Creating an account with the username of a deleted one is rejected (v1.2.1 code, `_create_local_user_no_commit`; not exercised by the evidence arm).
- **External accounts are not administered here.** Password reset and deletion refuse accounts that came from an external identity provider (v1.2.1 code, `reset_password` and `delete_user`; not exercised by the evidence arm).

capabilities.title: Authenticate automation with personal access tokens
capabilities.summary:
- **Mint, list, revoke.** `POST /auth/pats` creates a token, `GET /auth/pats` lists the caller's tokens (v1.2.1 code; the evidence checks the owner of the PATs it minted, not of every listed PAT), and `DELETE /auth/pats/{jti}` revokes one by its token id (v1.2.1 `kamiwaza/services/auth/api.py`: `create_pat`, `list_my_pats`, `revoke_my_pat`). Revocation is addressed to a specific token rather than resetting the user's credentials wholesale.
- **The PAT policy is readable.** `GET /auth/pat-config` (`get_pat_config`) reports the fixed lifetime bounds, the scope hierarchy and labels, and the scopes this caller may request with its default (v1.2.1 code). It reports the policy; it does not set it. The evidence checks the lifetime bounds, the offered and hierarchy scopes, and the default scope for type and consistency, not their values. It does not read the labels.
- **The SDK treats PATs as the automation path.** `create_pat`, `list_pats`, and `revoke_pat` in `kamiwaza_sdk/services/auth.py` mirror the API, and SDK clients authenticate with a PAT instead of an interactive session.
conditions: In v1.2.1 the PAT policy is fixed in platform code, not an operator setting. Lifetimes run from 60 seconds to 365 days, with a 30-day default, and the scope hierarchy is admin, write, read. A caller may mint scopes only up to its own roles, or its own PAT's scope. `GET /auth/pat-config` reports this policy for the caller.
limits:
- **Documentation.** On the kamiwaza-docs `release/1.2.1` branch, `docs/docs/security/admin-guide.md` has a "Personal Access Tokens and Service Access" section, and `docs/sdk_versioned_docs/version-1.2.0/current/services/auth.md` has a "Personal Access Tokens" section. The platform source's own `kamiwaza/services/auth/README.md` (v1.2.1) describes PAT creation, listing without tokens, and revocation. The claims above cite the platform code and the SDK surface, and the SDK evidence under Coverage notes exercises part of them.
- **A PAT carries a scope, capped at the caller's own level** (v1.2.1 code: `_resolve_pat_scope_ceiling`). The evidence does not test that a lower scope restricts what a token can do, so treat a token as equivalent to its user for authorization purposes until that is established.
- **Revocation is per token, and this document does not establish propagation timing.** How quickly a revoked token stops being accepted is not characterised here.

capabilities.title: End sessions by logout and remove tracked sessions as an administrator
capabilities.summary:
- logout
- front-channel-logout
- revoke-session
- purge-subject-sessions
conditions: At Core develop 4d00746 the administrator session routes act on whichever session authority the deployment configures, in two branches. (1) DB authority: AUTH_WORKROOM_BINDING_BACKEND=db with the Keycloak auth provider (the shipped chart default, charts/core/values.yaml rebac.workroomBindingBackend db with rebac.sessionEnabled false). The routes delete DB runtime-token-state records and do not need the Redis session store. (2) Session-store authority: AUTH_WORKROOM_BINDING_BACKEND=session_store (the platform settings default). The routes need AUTH_REBAC_SESSION_ENABLED=true plus a Redis session URL, and both answer 503 session_store_disabled when the store is off. With DB authority and the store also enabled, both are acted on.

Statements marked v1.2.1 or measured describe the Azure 1.2.1 deployment or the frozen recovery build fd262bc and are retained as history. They are not statements about develop 4d00746, whose source is cited in declared_by.
The deployment runs with authentication enabled and the platform Keycloak reachable.
Deleting a session or purging a subject's sessions requires the platform admin role (AdminIdentityContext on both routes; the evidence arm runs these calls only as an administrator).
limits:
- **Removing a tracked session is not a credential cutoff.** Administrator record removal was exercised on the frozen develop recovery build, but no already-issued access-token cutoff is claimed. The token semantics below come from the v1.2.1 platform code unless marked measured or develop `4d00746`.
  - Request authentication does not require a session record. ForwardAuth reads the record only to find the session's workroom binding (`_read_session_workroom`) and treats a missing record as no binding. An access token issued before the removal therefore stays valid until it expires; on the Azure 1.2.1 deployment access tokens were issued for 14400 seconds (measured, research probe S4).
  - Token refresh goes to Keycloak without consulting the session store, and a successful refresh writes the record again (`refresh_token` and `persist_session`).
  - Removal is not without effect. With `AUTH_WORKROOM_BINDING_BACKEND=session_store` (the settings default), resolving a runtime session from a platform token fails with `BINDING_LOST` when that session's record is missing (v1.2.1 `workrooms/session.py`). Under DB authority at develop `4d00746` the removed records are the ones browser child sessions and runtime launches read for their parent (`browser_sessions/parents.py`, `browser_sessions/runtime.py`). Which requests either effect reaches is not characterized here.
  - Do not present administrator session removal as ending a compromised or offboarded user's access.
- **The SDK's `logout()` on a client holding only an access token left the refresh token usable.**
  - Measured on the Azure deployment: `logout()` on such a client left the refresh token usable. The access token also kept working, while the response reported `session_termination_requested: true` (research probe S7; SDK test `test_sdk_logout_revokes_refresh_token`, a strict expected failure).
  - Such a client supplies no refresh token or ID-token cookie, so v1.2.1 sends Keycloak only the access token (as the `token` form field).
  - On the client that signed in, the refresh token stopped working after `logout()` (2026-09-17 probe, above). That the login response's cookies reached the logout request is inferred: the probe saw the cookie jar before and after, not the request.
  - v1.2.1 also forwards an ID-token cookie or body field as `id_token_hint` (`_collect_logout_tokens`). Whether a logout carrying only that hint ends the session was not measured.
- **There is no direct per-session read through the API.** A subject purge removes what it reads. The frozen recovery arm observes independent counts and complementary delete/logout checks in both orderings. This detects wrong-oldest/wrong-newest and over-deletion errors; it is not an independent per-record inspection and still assumes successful login persistence.
- **The counts assume every login wrote its record.** In v1.2.1, persisting a password login's session record is best effort. A store failure is logged, and the login still succeeds (`persist_session`). If one of a step's two sessions was never recorded, that step's purge count can match without the delete or logout having removed anything.

capabilities.title: Register and search datasets and containers in the data catalog
capabilities.summary:
- **Datasets are URN-identified entities.** `POST /catalog/datasets/` (201) registers a dataset — name, platform, environment, tags, properties, an optional schema, and an optional parent container — and returns its URN; the URN is the stable address every other surface uses. Dataset schemas read and write through dedicated endpoints, addressable by URN in three styles (path-embedded, query-parameter, and legacy path).
- **Containers group datasets.** Containers are logical groupings with URNs of their own: `POST /catalog/containers/` (201) creates one, `GET /catalog/containers/` lists and searches them, and membership endpoints add and remove datasets.
- **Finding data is a query, not a walk.** The dataset and container list endpoints take a free-text search query; on the DataHub implementation the search runs against the catalog index and results are post-filtered to the caller's workroom, since the index cannot filter on the platform's workroom property itself.
- **The registry is governed, and how strongly depends on one flag.** Every route requires an authenticated user; reads and writes run under workroom contexts, and a cross-workroom create or upsert answers 409. Those hold unconditionally. The ReBAC layer above them does not: **when `AUTH_REBAC_ENABLED` is on**, dataset creation assigns the creator as ReBAC owner and listing applies per-caller ReBAC visibility filtering, so what a caller finds is what the caller may see. **The flag defaults to off**, and with it off the list route returns before the visibility filter and no owner tuple is written — listing is then scoped by the caller's workroom read context alone. Workroom scoping is the floor; per-caller ReBAC filtering is opt-in.
- **The backing store is pluggable without changing the contract.** The default implementation is DataHub; kamiwaza-lite deployments run the platform's own database-backed implementation behind the same routes. Operations a backend does not implement answer 501 rather than misbehaving.
- **The SDK ships two dataset clients over one capability.** The catalog client covers the full legacy surface — datasets, containers, schema mutations, catalog secrets — with typed models; the federation-aware datasets client covers a minimal create/get/delete slice that returns federation-shaped references and adds attribute-gate binding. The duplication is an SDK-shape observation the inventory records, not two capabilities.
conditions: Every catalog route requires an authenticated user; reads run under a workroom read context and writes under a workroom write context.
The catalog backend is reachable — DataHub by default, or the platform's own database implementation in kamiwaza-lite mode.
limits:
- Attribute-gate binding on datasets is administered through this catalog's URNs but is claimed and documented as part of `authz.rebac-access-control`. Secrets storage alongside the catalog is a separate concern that has no capability document yet, so it is claimed nowhere in the kit — treat it as uncharacterized rather than as documented elsewhere.
- The SDK's dataset-publisher calls (`add_publisher`, `remove_publisher`) and `register_from_spec` have no server-side route at the pinned platform revision — an SDK-ahead-of-platform drift recorded here so the claim is not repeated from the SDK surface. Publishers are therefore not part of this capability's claim despite appearing in the inventory summary.
- The docs page states container creation and membership changes require admin permissions; the code requires a workroom write context, not an explicit admin check. Where they disagree, this document follows the code.

capabilities.title: Register S3 and PostgreSQL sources, then scan into the governed catalog
capabilities.summary:
- register
- list registered sources
- scan
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
SourceRegistrationRequest closes source types to s3/postgres. Connections carry catalog secret references, not raw credentials; registration does not materialize data (`content_materialized` is always false). Distinct from connector manifest administration and generic catalog dataset CRUD.

Authorization has an unconditional part and a conditional part, read at Core develop `4d00746`:

- **Always enforced.** `POST /ingestion/ingest/register` and `POST /ingestion/ingest/run` require an authenticated user. The workroom comes from the server-owned requester context, and a request that names a different workroom is rejected. For a non-Global target workroom, the service layer rechecks the requester's identity, current membership, and tenant agreement before registering or scanning (`_authorize_scoped_execution`). Global or unscoped context normalizes to no scoped workroom and bypasses that service-layer membership/tenant check; the route's authentication dependency still applies.
- **Enforced only when ReBAC is enabled.** The ingestion-admin requirement is a ReBAC object guard on the group `urn:li:group:ingestion-admins` (overridable with `INGESTION_ADMIN_GROUP_URN`). `_authorize_ingestion_admin` returns without checking when `AUTH_REBAC_ENABLED` is off, which is the platform default, and global admins bypass the group check when it is on.
- **Consequence.** On a deployment with ReBAC disabled, any authenticated caller passing the applicable context checks can register and scan a source (current membership is required for a non-Global target, not for Global or unscoped context); do not describe these routes as ingestion-admin-only there. The route's own declared grant model (`_SOURCE_REGISTRATION_BEHAVIOR`: "ingestion-admin authority plus current membership") therefore holds only with ReBAC enabled. Whether a ReBAC-off deployment should require an administrator role is a product decision recorded as open; it is not claimed here.

Listing registered sources (`GET /catalog/containers/registered-sources`) runs under a requested-workroom read context, is tenant-scoped, and omits secret-reference properties from the page. The kamiwaza-lite container manager's listing was not read.

capabilities.summary:

conditions: Secrets are addressed by URN. Retrieval of one secret is by URN; a list route with an optional free-text query also exists and returns metadata only.
limits:

capabilities.title: Manage file content inside platform-managed datasets
capabilities.summary:
- upload
- list
- read content
- conditional replace
- tombstone
- admin force-purge
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
This capability manages dataset manifests, revisions and stored content, unlike the metadata-only `catalog.dataset-registry` or workroom raw-file store. It is enabled by default but requires a healthy file/object backend. POST never replaces an existing live path; PUT requires `If-Match`. Default limits are 100 MiB per item, 2 GiB per dataset and 10,000 objects, with seven-day tombstone retention. Non-secret workroom S3 override redirects are disabled by default. Creating a writable dataset is role-gated (`admin,user` by default).

Delete creates a tombstone and does not remove bytes; a conditional replace likewise retires the superseded bytes rather than deleting them inline. Read at Core develop `4d00746`, retired bytes are physically purged by whichever of three paths comes first:

- **Retention elapsed.** The background reconciliation loop purges an item once its `purge_eligible_at` (tombstone time plus `WRITABLE_DATASET_TOMBSTONE_DAYS`, seven by default) has passed.
- **Consumer acknowledgement, before retention elapses.** The same background loop purges an item early once every consumer that has acknowledged the dataset has acknowledged the revision at which the item was retired (`purge_eligible`, `consumer_ack_floor`). A dataset no consumer has ever acknowledged never releases early. After seven days, unacknowledged retired content becomes eligible for purge; deletion still depends on the asynchronous reconciler and successful backend operations. Retention is neither a guaranteed minimum recovery window (acknowledgements can permit earlier deletion) nor a guaranteed deletion deadline (delays or failures can retain bytes longer).
- **Audited administrator force-purge.** `POST .../purge` requires a verified administrator, accepts only tombstoned items, and writes an audit record.

Retired-but-unpurged content counts toward the dataset byte and object limits: an upload can be refused with 413 (`wait for tombstone cleanup`) while retained history fills the cap, even though the live content is under it.

capabilities.title: Configure and manage governed data-source connectors
capabilities.summary:
- **Admin-gated creation with an observable deployment lifecycle.** `POST /connectors/` (201) creates a connector configuration from a registered connector type; the route requires admin identity and carries a declared admin-only policy behavior (`connector_config` resource, admin-only grant model). When the type's manifest ships a deployable workload, deployment is kicked off in the background and the connector's card moves `not_deployed` → `deploying` → `ready` on its own; the status vocabulary also includes `degraded` and `unknown`. Invalid configuration fails with 400.
- **Secrets are write-only.** Connector responses never include the client secret or service token — credential material is stored encrypted and stays server-side; what reads back is non-sensitive configuration and status.
- **A typed catalog populates onboarding.** `GET /connectors/catalog` (admin) lists connector types available to subscribe, merged from two sources deduplicated by type: the published remote catalog (`connectors.json` fetched per deployment version, with a `file://` override for air-gapped installs) and types registered into the DB-backed catalog, with the DB entry winning on conflict. Each entry is a self-describing connector manifest, validated on the way through, and flagged when the deployment is already subscribed.
- **New types and running instances both register first-class.** `POST /connectors/catalog` registers a connector *type* from its manifest — no workload deployed, no configuration stored — which is the SDK's `register_type`. `POST /connectors/register` (201) self-registers a connector already running at an endpoint: the platform fetches the connector's self-describing manifest from `GET {endpoint}/manifest` and subscribes it with the supplied (encrypted) configuration; routing and per-user verification gate on a non-null workload principal, so an instance can be registered before it is made routable.
- **Analysts see a governed availability surface, not the admin surface.** `GET /connectors/available` requires only an authenticated user and returns non-sensitive metadata for connectors that are enabled, fully configured, and actually stood up (`status` not `not_deployed`) — sync-seeded entries an admin has not deployed stay hidden. A per-connector `user_connectable` flag distinguishes connectors with per-user accounts from service-token or credential-less connectors, which present as status cards without a connect action.
- **Connection health is probed through the deployed connector.** `POST /connectors/{id}/verify` performs a real read through the platform's proxy using the calling user's own token, maps per-capability results with permanent-versus-transient classification, and persists the verdict on the user's connection (degrading it, marking `needs_reauth`, or healing it back to `connected` on positive proof). It answers 503 when the connector is not yet deployed. Note this is user-scoped verification of the caller's own connection — see `not_supported`.
- **Maintenance is part of the same surface.** Update, delete, explicit deploy, and remote-catalog sync are admin routes alongside create, so the fleet is maintained where it is created.
conditions: Creating, registering, updating, deleting, and deploying connectors are admin operations; the catalog listing is admin-only as well.

Catalog-driven onboarding depends on a reachable published connector catalog (the hosted `connectors.json` for the deployment's version, or a `file://` override for air-gapped installs) or on connector types registered directly into the DB-backed catalog.
limits:
- The connector routes are mounted unconditionally — there is no feature gate to enable; the gate is admin identity (resolved from forwarded-auth headers or Keycloak tokens).
- The catalog's provider set is deployment-dependent. The platform source names no providers; Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace are established by the product documentation (which also lists Dropbox as "Coming Soon" — not claimable), and any other entry is whatever the deployment's catalog or DB registrations carry.
- Workroom-scoped connector surfaces (listing a workroom's connector catalog, browsing and searching sources) exist as separate user-facing routes; this capability claims the management surface. Per-user authorization and account connection are `connectors.user-oauth-authorization`.
- This area is sometimes called "Data Shed" in requirements material; that vocabulary does not appear in the product, whose shipped surface is "Data Connectors". The mapping is on behavior, not name — a recorded finding.

capabilities.title: Per-tool OAuth operation policies
capabilities.summary:
- create a tool policy (`POST /oauth-broker/policies/`)
- read a tool policy by ID (`GET /oauth-broker/policies/{policy_id}`)
- list tool policies, optionally filtered by app or tool (`GET /oauth-broker/policies/`)
- update a policy's allowed operations, allowed scope subset or metadata (`PATCH /oauth-broker/policies/{policy_id}`)
- delete a tool policy (`DELETE /oauth-broker/policies/{policy_id}`)
- enforce the allowed operations before a call on the broker's standard proxy path (and at legacy ephemeral token minting), answering 403 on a violation
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
On by default, API only. The OAuth broker router is mounted with no feature flag, and the policy routes sit under it at `/oauth-broker/policies`. No SDK method calls these routes. The UI source holds only generated API types for them; no shipped UI screen was found.

Creating, reading, changing or deleting a policy requires the caller to own its app installation or to be an administrator; anyone else gets 403, and an unknown policy id gets 404 before that check. A list request without an app filter returns every policy to an administrator and only the policies of the caller's own app installations to anyone else.

Enforcement denies by default. A proxied call is refused unless the tool is in the app installation's `allowed_tools`, a policy exists for that app, tool and provider, and the requested operation is in the policy's `allowed_operations`. A tool with no policy for a provider cannot make any call to that provider through the standard proxy.

The check runs on the broker's standard proxy path (`/oauth-broker/proxy/{provider}/{service}/{operation}`) and on legacy ephemeral token minting, where it is checked as the operation `token.mint`. The delegated-workload execution path does not call it; that path authorizes each call with a one-use lease instead. Policies govern those two broker paths only, not tool execution in general. The broker's connector routes (`POST /oauth-broker/connectors/{connector_id}/proxy` and `/identity-proxy`, and `POST /oauth-broker/tokens/connectors/{connector_id}/mint`) do not check tool policies (`kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/api/connector_proxy.py:34`, `kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/api/connector_proxy.py:38`, `kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/api/tokens.py:37`, `kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/api/tokens.py:152`). All three require the caller to be the connector's bound workload (`kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/connector_token_service.py:245`). The two proxy routes also enforce the connector's egress allowlist (`kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/connector_proxy_service.py:68`, `kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/connector_proxy_service.py:109`). The mint route has no egress check: it checks the requested scopes against the granted ones and returns the provider token to the connector (`kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/connector_token_service.py:177`, `kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/connector_token_service.py:114`). For a per-user connection that token is the connection's own provider token, not narrowed to the requested scopes; the scopes are recorded on the lease and returned as `granted_scopes` (`kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/connector_token_service.py:178`, `kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/connector_token_service.py:101`, `kamiwaza/services/oauth_broker/connector_token_service.py:116`).

Operation names come from the broker's registered operation list. At this revision only Google operations are registered: Gmail (`gmail.search`, `gmail.getMessage`, `gmail.send`, `gmail.listLabels`, `gmail.modify`), Drive (`drive.listFiles`, `drive.getFile`) and Calendar (`calendar.list`, `calendar.events`). The create route stores the submitted operation names without checking them against that list.

A read-only Gmail tool is possible: a policy that lists `gmail.search` and `gmail.getMessage` but not `gmail.send` refuses sends. The email tool deployment does not start that way. When the tool service provisions OAuth for an email tool, it creates a policy for `email-mcp` that allows `gmail.send` and `gmail.modify`. An owner must update that policy to make the tool read-only.

`allowed_scope_subset` is checked only when a legacy ephemeral token is minted, and an empty list places no limit there. The proxy path does not check it.
