capabilities.title: Authorize personal data-source access with OAuth/OIDC brokering
capabilities.summary:
- **The connect flow is manifest-driven, not provider-hardcoded.** `POST /connectors/{id}/connect` (any authenticated user) begins connecting the caller's account per the connector's declared flow: authorization-code connectors return `{"auth_url": ...}` for a browser redirect, device-code connectors return an RFC 8628 device-authorization payload (`user_code`, `verification_uri`, poll interval), and the client branches. A connector holding a shared or public credential answers 409 — there is no per-user account to connect.
- **Device-code completion is pollable and provider-polite.** `POST /connectors/{id}/connect/poll` reports `pending`, `connected`, or `expired` for a device-code flow, with server-side throttling that honors the provider's interval and `slow_down` responses. On success, tokens are stored and the user's connection record moves to `connected`.
- **The public callback is state-driven and replay-resistant.** `GET /connectors/public/{provider}/callback` is deliberately unauthenticated — the request is the provider's redirect — and routing is carried entirely by a single-use CSRF `state` (5-minute TTL) that identifies connector and user and is consumed before the code exchange, so a state cannot be replayed. The exchange runs as a confidential client; the response is a popup page that messages the opener and closes.
- **Tokens stay server-side, per user.** The token payload is written to the platform's secret store under a per-connector, per-user key, and the user's connection record carries status, granted scopes, expiry, and (best-effort) the external account email. Connector API responses never return the tokens.
- **Connection health is a first-class, per-user verdict.** `GET /connectors/{id}/connection` reports the caller's connection including failing capabilities; `POST /connectors/{id}/verify` probes a real read through the deployed connector with the caller's own token, classifies per-capability failures as permanent versus transient, and persists the verdict — degrading the connection, marking it `needs_reauth`, or healing it back to `connected` on positive proof.
- **Downstream access is brokered, leased, and revocable.** The OAuth broker's connector-scoped mint releases a provider access token only to the workload principal bound to the connector's subscription, on presentation of the acting user's verified subject token — on-behalf-of, not impersonation — with the refresh token and client secret never leaving the platform core and every mint lease-tracked for revoke-on-disconnect. The broker's application-scoped mint (`POST /oauth-broker/tokens/mint`) applies the same discipline for App Garden tool installations: ephemeral tokens with 1-to-15-minute broker leases, an optional scope subset of the connection's granted scopes, lease status and revoke endpoints, and an explicit steer toward the proxy mode that never exposes tokens at all. Disconnecting an account revokes its outstanding broker leases.
conditions: An admin has configured and deployed the connector; the connect flow answers 409 when the connector uses a shared or public credential (there is no per-user account to connect) and verification answers 503 until the connector workload is deployed.
The user's browser and the platform can reach the identity provider; the provider's app registration lists the platform's public callback path as a redirect URI.
limits:
- A broker lease expiring or being revoked does not guarantee provider-side token invalidation — the code states this itself: provider token lifetime is controlled by the provider and may outlive the broker lease if provider-side revocation fails.
- The connect flow acquires and stores tokens in the connectors service; the broker's role is downstream — mint, lease, refresh, proxy, and lease revocation on disconnect — not the acquisition handshake.
- The product documentation describes the redirect flow for users; the device-code path is exercised by the Microsoft 365 journey scenario but is not documented on the docs page. Neither the OAuth broker nor its endpoints have a docs page — a recorded docs-gap finding.
- The redirect URI the provider must allow is the platform's fixed public callback path (`/api/connectors/public/{provider}/callback`), derived from the platform's external URL.

capabilities.title: Pending-approval queue for delegated actions
capabilities.summary:
- list the effects waiting for approval in a tenant (`GET /api/v1/delegated-workloads/effects/pending-approval?tenant_id=...`, SDK `DelegatedApprovalAPI.list_pending`)
- watch the queue by polling it (SDK `DelegatedApprovalAPI.watch_pending`)
- approve or deny a pending effect (`POST /api/v1/delegated-workloads/effects/{effect_id}/approval`, SDK `DelegatedApprovalAPI.decide`); this decision route is also described in `delegation.consent-and-approval-gates`
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
Default state depends on how Core is configured. The delegated-workload contract is published by default (`DELEGATED_WORKLOADS_ENABLED`, default `true`). The effect routes, including this queue, are added only when Core builds the delegated authority runtime. Core's own settings hold that runtime by default. `DELEGATED_WORKLOADS_ALLOWED_RETURN_URI_PREFIXES` defaults to empty, and while it is empty the runtime is not built. The signing-key, run-reference-key, nonce-secret, issuer and audience settings also default to empty, and with all five empty the runtime is held too. With the runtime held, the queue path is not published at all.

The core Helm chart in `deploy` fills in the key paths and the return prefix by default. `delegatedWorkloads.enabled` defaults to `true`. When it is enabled, the chart renders the signing-key and run-reference-key paths, and an empty return-prefix list becomes `https://<global.domain>`. The render fails if `global.domain` is empty. This batch did not trace a default Helm install end to end to a built runtime. A deployment that runs Core without these settings gets no queue.

Only approvers can read the queue. The caller needs a signed-in member session whose roles include `admin` or `it_approver`; any other member gets `approver_authority_required`. The `tenant_id` in the request must be the caller's own tenant, or the call fails with `approver_tenant_unavailable`. The list holds the effects in that tenant whose decision is pending approval and whose status is reserved, oldest first.

A decision needs the same approver roles and a valid `X-CSRF-Token` header. The request names the effect digest, the policy version and `approve` or `deny`.

Watching is client-side polling. `watch_pending` is a generator that lists the queue, then sleeps. The interval must be positive and defaults to 5 seconds. There is no server push and no notification.

The SDK class `kamiwaza_sdk.delegated_workloads.DelegatedApprovalAPI` is built from a base URL and a member session.

The existing `delegation.consent-and-approval-gates` document says there is no pending-decision queue. At these revisions that is out of date for the API and SDK. That document is unchanged by this batch.

capabilities.title: Track delegated work as claimed runs with explicit, recorded state transitions
capabilities.summary:
- **Reserve, then claim.** `POST /runs` reserves a run (`execution_routes.py:165`) and `POST /run-claims` claims it (`:196`). The two steps are distinct, so work that was authorized but never picked up is distinguishable from work that started.
- **Transitions are explicit.** `POST /run-claims/{claim_id}/transitions` (`:228`) records state movement, with a second route on the same path carrying job heartbeats (`:258`) — a claim that stops heartbeating is detectable rather than silently stuck. Claim deadlines and successor handling are their own modules (`claim_deadlines.py`, `claim_successors.py`), as is the persistence and transaction behavior underneath (`claim_persistence.py`, `claim_lease_persistence.py`, `claim_transactions.py`).
- **Cancellation is a first-class transition.** `POST /runs/{run_id}/cancellation` (`:388`) is a recorded action, not an abandonment.
- **Effects are reserved before they occur.** `POST /runs/{run_id}/effects` (`:419`) reserves an intended effect, which is what makes an approval gate possible at all (see `delegation.consent-and-approval-gates`). `POST /runs/{run_id}/capability` (`:341`) resolves the capability a run is exercising.
- **The SDK carries both halves.** `DelegatedControlPlaneClient.reserve_run` (`client.py:82`) drives the control plane; `executor.py` is the executing side.
conditions: The claiming workload is attested and holds capability material for the run it claims — see `delegation.workload-identity-and-attestation`.
A run is reserved before it is claimed; a claim is against an existing reservation, not a free-floating assertion of work.
limits:
- **No documentation page describes this**, and there is no UI. Claims rest on platform code and the SDK.
- **A lifecycle is not a scheduler.** Nothing here places work, enforces quotas, prioritizes, or preempts. Those appear in requirements material and have no implementation source.
- **Heartbeating detects a stalled claim; it does not recover one.** Deadline and successor modules exist, but this document does not claim a tested failover or graceful-degradation story — that would need evidence it does not have.

capabilities.title: Build, deploy, and publish custom extensions with the kz-ext toolchain
capabilities.summary:
- Scaffold an extension of type `app`, `tool` or `service` with `kz-ext create`.
- Run the remote iterate loop with `kz-ext dev`: build a development image with a new revision tag, push it, create or patch the extension on the connected instance, and poll until the deployment settles.
- Create, list, read, read the status of, patch and delete an extension through the platform's `/extensions` API and the SDK's `ExtensionService`.
- Publish an extension's catalog entry with `kz-ext publish`, in a supported catalog schema.
conditions: The iterate loop works against a live cluster — it builds and pushes a development image tagged with a new revision, creates or patches the extension with that revision, and polls the deployment.
Pushing a development image presupposes a reachable image registry the cluster can pull from.

How the platform holds a created extension depends on the extension runtime the install selected. The umbrella chart default is the direct runtime (core.extensionRuntime.mode direct, extensionOperator.enabled false), which installs no KamiwazaExtension CRD; the operator runtime is an explicit opt-in.
limits:
- **The runtime decides what "platform resource" means.** Do not quote this capability as "extensions are Kubernetes custom resources" without naming the runtime. That is true where the extension operator is enabled and false on the default direct-runtime install. Core itself falls back to the operator runtime when `KAMIWAZA_EXTENSION_RUNTIME_MODE` is unset; the direct default is set by the umbrella chart.
- **Evidence stops at the scaffold.** Existing evidence in this area demonstrates scaffold generation and the runtime contract being honored. The `kz-ext dev` deploy, the local development loop, and validation are documented and probed by hand, not established by collected evidence.
- **This is the developer's path, and the persona vocabulary does not have a developer.** The inherited persona vocabularies cover Admin, Non-admin user, Analyst, Operator, and SysAdmin; this capability genuinely serves a developer, and that mismatch is a signal to reconcile the vocabularies rather than a defect in this document.
- **Publishing is platform-local.** The extension becomes listable and runnable on the cluster it was published to. Nothing here distributes it further.
- **The command list is open.** At the cited SDK revision `kz-ext` also registers `catalog-capabilities`, `catalog-cap` and `catalog-remove`; they are named in the citation and are not part of the operations above.

capabilities.title: Pair Kamiwaza clusters into a governed federation
capabilities.summary:
- pair-federation
- inspect-federation
- select-identity-mode
- allowlist-brokered-subject
- diagnose-federation
- probe-peer-capabilities
- disconnect-federation
- strip-source-authority

`strip-source-authority` is claimed for the receiver-controlled `shared_idp` mode; under `peer_kc` the receiver forwards the source cluster's roles and attributes unchanged (see Conditions and limits). This document claims nothing for `receiver_realm`.
conditions: Two clusters with mutually reachable HTTPS endpoints, distinct display names, and distinct hostnames. The documented baseline names 1.3.0 on both sides.
Istio selected through the supported deployment values on both clusters, and gateway certificates whose SANs cover the hostnames used for Host and TLS SNI routing.
Pairing is a receiver-side decision. The cluster that receives calls (the grantor) chooses the federation's identity mode.
limits:
- **The documented baseline is version-matched.** Setup names 1.3.0 clusters on both sides. This document does not establish behavior for pairing across mismatched versions.
- **The deployment shape is constrained.** Istio and SAN-correct gateway certificates are prerequisites, not recommendations; hostname and SNI routing depend on them. A pairing attempt on a deployment that does not meet this will fail in the network layer rather than the federation layer.
- **`peer_kc` is a weaker posture and is documented as legacy.** It makes the source cluster an identity authority for the receiver: role stripping and token-derived attributes do not apply to it. New `peer_kc` pairings are refused unless the operator sets `ALLOW_UNTRUSTED_FEDERATION` (`kamiwaza/cluster/federation.py:645`). Where a customer asks which trust model is in use, the answer matters — do not present federation generically as "receiver-controlled" without saying which mode a deployment runs.
- **Attribute changes are eventually consistent, bounded by token lifetime.** For a customer whose threat model includes prompt revocation of a clearance, this is a real limit and should be stated rather than discovered.

capabilities.title: Enforce receiver-side policy on federated work with execution gates
capabilities.summary:
- install-gate-package
- discover-gate
- bind-cluster-execution-gate
- read-cluster-execution-gate
- clear-cluster-execution-gate
- gate-before-dispatch
- deny-unconfigured-mesh
- allow-unconfigured-local
- deny-on-unknown-decision

Binding an attribute gate to a dataset is `authz.rebac-access-control`'s `bind-dataset-attribute-gate`, not an operation of this capability.
conditions: Three layers can set the gate and the first that holds a value wins — an API binding written by `PUT /api/cluster/execution-gate`, the `AUTHZ_EXECUTION_GATE` environment variable, and the Helm value core.authz.executionGate.{type, config}, which the chart renders into the core-runtime-config ConfigMap.
limits:
- **With no gate configured, fail-closed applies only to the mesh direction.** An unconfigured cluster still allows local submissions. That is deliberate and documented, but it follows that having execution gates does not by itself mean any policy is being enforced on local users. Once a configuration layer holds a gate setting, an UNKNOWN decision — a gate that fails to load, raises while evaluating, or whose setting does not resolve to a gate — is refused for local and mesh submissions alike, because `JobGateRunner.pre_dispatch` applies no source check on that path.
- **A malformed `config` member is not refused.** When a gate setting names a gate but its `config` is not an object, the setting still resolves: the named gate is loaded with an empty config (`{}`) in place of the malformed one, and the substitution is only logged as a warning (`ClusterAuthzConfig._parse` in `kamiwaza/services/authz/gates/config.py`; `JobGateRunner.pre_dispatch` passes the parsed config to the gate). Whether jobs are then admitted is decided by how the named gate behaves with an empty config; a gate that raises while being constructed is refused with `gate_load_error`.
- **The gate can be bound at runtime, and a deployment-time gate can only be changed at deployment.** A native-realm administrator sets and clears the cluster's gate with `PUT` and `DELETE /api/cluster/execution-gate`. Reading it with `GET` requires an authenticated user and the cluster-viewer gate, which admits authenticated users when ReBAC is disabled and authorized viewers when it is enabled (`kamiwaza/services/authz/gates/api.py:754`, `:820`, `:856`); the SDK exposes these as `set_execution_gate`, `get_execution_gate` and `clear_execution_gate` (`kamiwaza_sdk/services/cluster_federation.py:122`, `:138`, `:143`). The API binding is the first of three layers, ahead of the `AUTHZ_EXECUTION_GATE` environment variable and the Helm value (`kamiwaza/services/authz/gates/config.py:17`). So an operator can tighten or replace policy without a redeploy. The limit that remains: clearing the API binding does not remove a gate that comes from the environment variable or the chart, which then becomes active again and is changed only by editing the Deployment or upgrading the release.
- **This is the coarse gate.** It answers "may this caller run jobs here". It does not answer "what may they see". A customer who hears "execution gates" and understands record-level policy has misunderstood; the attribute gates on datasets are the other half and are a separate concern.

capabilities.title: Submit and monitor jobs on federated clusters
capabilities.summary:
- **The job surface is a complete lifecycle.** `POST /cluster/jobs/submit` (201) submits asynchronously and returns the job id; `POST /cluster/jobs/run` (200) blocks to completion or timeout; list, status, result, logs, and cancel round it out. Failure semantics are typed: a gate denial is 403 with the gate named, a result requested before success is 409, expired engine logs are 410, an engine-dashboard failure is 502, and an on-behalf-of token problem distinguishes 401 from 503.
- **A job is a bounded, sanitized execution.** The entrypoint is a shell command run as a Ray job with a timeout (1 second to 24 hours) that auto-cancels — a timed-out synchronous run terminates as `STOPPED` with `timed_out: true` rather than hanging. Structured results travel by a log-marker protocol the job prints. The server strips every runtime-environment key except environment variables as a deliberate supply-chain safeguard, because the job inherits the submitter's platform token.
- **Execution and release are both gate-checked.** Submission runs the cluster's execution gate before dispatch — authorization happens before any compute is spent, and a deny or unknown answers 403. Result retrieval record-filters gated target datasets against the caller's identity attributes before release. With ReBAC enabled, job reads and cancels require an executor-class relation (auto-granted to the submitter); mesh-origin callers see only their own source cluster's jobs.
- **Cross-cluster transport is paired, signed, and receiver-controlled.** Remote calls travel the mesh proxy (`/api/mesh/{cluster}/cluster/jobs/...`) to a `PAIRED` federation only. The envelope is HMAC-signed with the pairing's preshared key over the source cluster, user, roles, route, and the hash of the forwarded caller JWT; the receiver validates the caller's own token against the shared keys, allowlists which brokered users may act, strips source-asserted cluster roles, and enforces its own ReBAC and attribute gates — cross-cluster authorization is receiver-controlled by design, with loop and hop-limit protection (508) on the proxy.
- **The SDK makes remote jobs a branch, not an exception.** `run` returns a typed job result synchronously — a failed job is a result with `status: FAILED` to branch on, not an exception — and its recoverable mode composes `submit_async` plus `wait` so the job id is in hand from the start. `wait` polls status with capped backoff to a terminal state, tolerates a 410 no-marker result while keeping status authoritative, and raises a typed timeout; `cancel` stops a job; a 401 mid-flight gets one token refresh and retry, and pairing-propagation delays are retried on their own schedule before raising a typed pairing timeout.
conditions: Remote execution reaches only a federation in `PAIRED` status; the mesh proxy answers 404 for any other target and 400 for a target that resolves to the local cluster.
The initiating cluster can reach the peer's ingress over TLS (optionally with a pinned peer CA); the pairing's per-federation preshared key signs the mesh envelope.
limits:
- **The SDK's `target_cluster` argument routes through the mesh proxy.** At `kamiwaza-sdk@6e98706`, `JobRouter.request` uses the local `/cluster/jobs/{endpoint}` path only when `target_cluster` is `None`; otherwise it sends the request to `/mesh/{selector}/api/cluster/jobs/{endpoint}` with the federation credential headers (`kamiwaza_sdk/services/jobs_routing.py:20`). `target_cluster` is a routing argument and is not placed in the request body (`kamiwaza_sdk/services/jobs_federation.py:185`). A blank, padded or path-unsafe selector is rejected before any request is made (`jobs_routing.py:55`). `submit_async` remembers the target for a bounded number of recent job ids on the same client, so later `wait`, `cancel` and result calls need `target_cluster` again only from a different client or after that cache has rolled over. The previously cited SDK revision `971ed14` already contains this mesh-routing behavior; no older-version cutoff is established here.
- The SDK's convenience arguments for pip packages, Python modules, and working directories are stripped server-side along with the rest of the runtime environment (only environment variables survive); the docs' submit example showing a pip list contradicts the shipped behavior, and the code wins.
- The docs page states admin authentication as a prerequisite; the code requires an authenticated user plus the gate and executor checks, not the admin role.
- Inter-cluster trust is preshared-key HMAC plus forwarded-token validation over TLS — not mutual-TLS client certificates between clusters.
- Three adjacent concerns sit outside this capability: establishing the cluster pairing (`federation.cluster-pairing`), the receiver's execution policy (`federation.execution-gates`), and moving data rather than compute, which has no capability document and is uncharacterized in the kit rather than claimed elsewhere.

capabilities.title: Extract text and transcripts from images, audio, and video during ingestion
capabilities.summary:
- Discover the configured supported file-type surface and distinguish built-in extraction from OmniParse routing.
- Query audio readiness for a workroom, including opt-in MIME checks and typed remediation.
- Extract searchable text from a representative image through OmniParse.
- Transcribe a representative audio input through OmniParse.
- Extract transcript and selected-keyframe text from a representative video with both required model connections.
- Report file extraction failure when media processing is unavailable or required model configuration is missing.

These operations define the proposed review scope; they are not a claim that a live verification arm has passed. File-size and timeout boundaries remain conditions that require boundary evidence separately.
conditions: OmniParse is the parsing and transcription extension; it runs as its own service (a workroom-scoped instance is lazily provisioned when the platform manages it locally, or an operator points the context service at a deployed endpoint). The audio-readiness probe exists precisely because it can be absent, unreachable, or unconfigured.

The pipeline routes a file through OmniParse when the extraction configuration enables it (`use_omniparse`), or when OmniParse is available for the workroom and the file type has no built-in extractor (auto-enable). The context service's connector-import bridge sets `use_omniparse` per batch.

Audio and video transcription need a transcription model, either configured (workroom-scoped OmniParse config or global settings) or auto-linked from a platform model. Without one, audio fails readiness and video analysis raises.
Video analysis additionally needs a vision model, either supplied on the request (`vision_model`), configured, or auto-linked. Without one the video file fails; there is no audio-only fallback.
limits:
- The service guide claims OCR- and vision-oriented extraction and audio/video transcription; it names no specific OCR or transcription engines and makes no language-detection claim. Engine names appear only as platform configuration defaults, so this document does not claim them as product behavior.
- Extraction quality and modality coverage are OmniParse's; this document claims the routing, readiness, and limit contract the platform sources establish, and `context.workroom-document-search` claims what happens to the extracted text afterward.
- **Media failures are fatal to the file, in every mode.** For audio and video, an OmniParse outage, a failed transcription or analysis call, a missing model, an empty transcript (service path), or an empty video-analysis result fails that file with a typed error; `strict_omniparse=false` does not turn these into a silent fallback, because no built-in extractor exists for media. A remote-source import also does not degrade a media file to "import only".
- **Non-strict fallback is limited to document types with a built-in extractor.** With `strict_omniparse=false` (the schema default), a `.txt`/`.md`/`.docx` file falls back to the built-in extractor on an OmniParse failure; a `.pdf` falls back only on a transient (non-unreachable, non-auth) failure; image files, which have no built-in extractor, raise. With `strict_omniparse=true`, every OmniParse failure raises.
- The platform has two ingestion code paths for media: the context service's pipeline service and a Ray worker module. The guarantees above are those of the pipeline service. The Ray worker module differs in two ways (it ignores `strict_omniparse`, and an empty audio transcript yields zero chunks, a `not_searchable` skipped file, rather than an error); no caller was found inside the Core source tree; external callers were not audited, so that search does not establish the helper as unreachable.

capabilities.title: Parse a document fetched from a public URL
capabilities.summary:
- submit a URL (`POST /v1/documents/from-url`)
- check the URL and every redirect against the fetch policy
- store the fetched document as a record
- read the stored document as Markdown or HTML (`GET /v1/documents/{doc_id}/markdown`, `GET /v1/documents/{doc_id}/html`)
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
OmniParse extension REST surface, not the Core ingestion pipeline. On by default: `URL_FETCH_ENABLE` defaults to `true` (`src/omniparse/settings.py:73`), and the extension manifest does not override it. When it is `false`, the request is refused (`src/omniparse/service/_service_url.py:80`). The OmniParse container needs outbound network access.

The fetch accepts only `http` and `https` (`src/omniparse/service/_public_url.py:26`), ports 80 and 443, and URLs without credentials. The host must resolve only to public addresses (`src/omniparse/service/_public_url.py:100`). Private, loopback and link-local addresses are rejected, so intranet URLs do not work. Every redirect is checked again, up to `URL_MAX_REDIRECTS` (default 10). Content is capped at `URL_MAX_SIZE_MB` (default 100) (`src/omniparse/settings.py:79`). The content type must be on the same `ALLOWED_MIME` list as uploads: PDF, DOCX, PPTX, HTML, plain text, Markdown and common image formats (`src/omniparse/settings.py:67`). `BLOCKED_DOMAINS` is empty by default.

The fetch stores the bytes and a record, and the heavy Docling conversion runs later, when an export or chunks are requested (`src/omniparse/facades/rest/app.py:343`). Requests need Kamiwaza authentication when `KAMIWAZA_USE_AUTH` is true (`src/omniparse/facades/rest/app.py:128`), which the manifest sets (`kamiwaza.json:59`). An MCP tool with the same name exists in a separately launched process (`python -m omniparse.facades.mcp.server`); `MCP_TRANSPORT=http` selects HTTP and otherwise it uses STDIO. That entry point is independent of `OMNIPARSE_MODE` (`src/omniparse/facades/mcp/server.py:1409`); combined mode only advertises the separate MCP process (`src/omniparse/main.py:119`). The manifest default remains `rest` (`kamiwaza.json:39`). The README's URL example posts JSON to `/v1/documents` (`README.md:104`). At this revision that route requires a multipart file (`src/omniparse/facades/rest/app.py:237`), so URL input goes to `/v1/documents/from-url`.

capabilities.title: Parse and apply source security markings during ingestion
capabilities.summary:
- index-document-with-marking
- list-indexed-documents
- read-indexed-document
conditions: The claims below cover documents entering through the DDE indexing surfaces (the documents API, connector-triggered ingest with seed documents, and the S3 ingestion worker); other entry paths are outside these sources.

Parsing, boundary evaluation and persistence of markings all require an operator-configured marking provider (KAMIWAZA_MARKINGS_ENABLED=true with KAMIWAZA_MARKINGS_PROVIDER and an optional profile). It is off by default in platform code and in the shipped chart (markings.enabled false). With no provider, provider-managed marking_text, connector defaults, and boundaries are refused and nothing is parsed. The deprecated security_marking-only input is accepted and stored verbatim without provider validation or enforcement.

Core carries no marking grammar or level vocabulary at develop 4d00746. Which marking strings parse, and into what, is defined entirely by the configured provider and its profile, which are outside the cited sources.
limits:
- **Off by default.** `KAMIWAZA_MARKINGS_ENABLED` defaults false in platform code and the chart ships `markings.enabled: false`. In that state `POST /dde/documents/` with `marking_text`, or against a connector that has a `level_boundary` or `default_marking`, answers 400 (`Markings are disabled; marked operations are unsupported`). The deprecated `security_marking` request field is then stored verbatim and never parsed or enforced.
- **No marking vocabulary is claimed.** Earlier revisions of this document listed CAPCO/ICISM classification levels, SCI controls, control markings, dissemination controls and `REL TO` handling as built-in parser coverage. That parser is not in core at develop `4d00746`; any such coverage now belongs to a separately distributed provider that the cited sources do not include. Do not describe specific marking formats to a customer from this document.
- **An unresolvable marking is now a governed 400, not a 500.** `MarkingError` derives from `ValueError` and the document-create route maps it to 400. The earlier recorded limit — an unrecognized leading classification surfacing as an unhandled 500 — described the removed parser and no longer applies. No rejection record is written for an unparseable marking; the `dde_security_rejection` record is written only for a boundary violation.
- **Seed-document and S3-worker ingest account for parsing failures per document.** Both paths catch boundary violations separately. A `MarkingError` (unparseable marking, or markings disabled) is also caught: seed ingestion handles it through `except ValueError` (`ingestion.py:141`), and the S3 worker through its `except Exception` safety net (`ingestion_workers/s3.py:103`). The item is counted as failed and the loop continues; an unparseable marking does not produce the boundary-violation `dde_security_rejection` event. The S3 worker passes no per-object marking, so objects take the connector's default marking.
- The claims cover the DDE indexing path named in the preconditions. These sources do not show the context-service upload pipeline or other entry paths passing through this evaluator; marking-aware behavior elsewhere is unestablished.
- A longer enforcement chain is demanded of this area — marking-aware context assembly and release minimization in downstream surfaces — with no implementation source behind it. That remains a recorded finding, owned by no entry.
- Documentation of the provider model (`docs/services/marking-providers.md`, referenced from the chart values) was not read for this revision; whether the published data-engine docs page still describes the removed system-high header and connector marking fields is an open docs-gap finding.

capabilities.title: Describe video keyframes with a vision model
capabilities.summary:
- submit a video analysis job, choosing I-frame or fixed-interval keyframe sampling, a keyframe cap, a simple or structured prompt, and per-request vision and transcription endpoint overrides
- poll job status
- extract keyframes and the audio track
- describe each keyframe with an OpenAI-compatible vision model
- transcribe the audio track
- retrieve the combined analysis, the transcript (JSON or Markdown), the keyframe descriptions, and a single keyframe image
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
This is the OmniParse extension's REST API (`src/omniparse/facades/rest/app.py:873`). Frame descriptions are off by default. `VISION_MODEL_ENABLE` defaults to `false` in code (`src/omniparse/settings.py:120`) and in the App Garden manifest (`kamiwaza.json:40`). If vision is disabled and the request passes no `vision_*` override, or if no vision endpoint is set, the description step raises an error (`src/omniparse/service/_service_video.py:372`, `src/omniparse/service/_service_video.py:385`) and the job is marked failed (`src/omniparse/service/_service_video.py:258`). Keyframe images are saved only inside that description step (`src/omniparse/service/_service_video.py:484`), so a job stopped by either check returns no frames.

A job also needs:

- ffmpeg and ffprobe in the container (`src/omniparse/service/_service_video.py:109`).
- Transcription enabled. `TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL_ENABLE` defaults to `true` (`src/omniparse/settings.py:166`) and is checked at submit time (`src/omniparse/service/_service_video.py:103`).
- A transcription endpoint that is configured, passed with the request or found by auto-discovery (`src/omniparse/service/_service_transcription.py:273`). The job resolves it even for a video with no audio track (`src/omniparse/service/_service_video.py:275`).

Defaults are I-frame sampling (`src/omniparse/settings.py:214`), a 5-second step in interval mode (`src/omniparse/settings.py:217`), at most 120 keyframes (`src/omniparse/settings.py:220`), the simple prompt style (`src/omniparse/settings.py:227`), a 500 MB upload cap (`src/omniparse/settings.py:205`) and an allowlist of MP4, QuickTime, Matroska, WebM, AVI and MPEG types (`src/omniparse/settings.py:210`). Job status is kept for one hour by default (`src/omniparse/settings.py:230`). The keyframe sampling modes are exactly `iframes` and `interval` (`src/omniparse/schemas.py:509`).

A configured vision model that fails is different: if the call fails on a frame, including because the model cannot be reached, that frame is still saved with an error object as its description, and the job completes (`src/omniparse/service/_service_video.py:481`, `src/omniparse/service/_service_video.py:543`). A failed transcription call is not: transcription runs before any keyframe is described (`src/omniparse/service/_service_video.py:232`), and when it fails, after any retries, the job is marked failed with no keyframe saved (`src/omniparse/service/_service_video.py:258`). A description is whatever the configured model returns for a short prompt about people, objects, actions and on-screen text (`src/omniparse/service/_service_video.py:84`), or for a JSON prompt in structured mode (`src/omniparse/service/_service_video.py:76`). This path does no face or identity matching. When a request overrides the vision endpoint with an untrusted host and supplies no key, the operator's vision key is not sent (`src/omniparse/adapters/transcription_adapter.py:435`).

The routes require Kamiwaza authentication by default. `KAMIWAZA_USE_AUTH` defaults to `true` (`src/omniparse/settings.py:280`) and the route dependency checks it (`src/omniparse/facades/rest/app.py:128`). A `GET /v1/video/analysis/status` route is registered after `GET /v1/video/analysis/{doc_id}` (`src/omniparse/facades/rest/app.py:1074`, `src/omniparse/facades/rest/app.py:1000`). With first-match routing the status path would go to the analysis lookup, so it is not listed as an operation. That is inferred from route order and was not run. An MCP tool for the same job exists (`src/omniparse/facades/mcp/server.py:949`), but the default mode serves REST only (`src/omniparse/main.py:155`).

The Core context ingestion worker also sends video files to this endpoint (`kamiwaza/services/context/pipeline/jobs/worker.py:238`, `kamiwaza/services/context/adapters/omniparse.py:1127`) and turns each described keyframe into a text chunk (`kamiwaza/services/context/pipeline/jobs/worker.py:393`). It fails the file when no vision model (`kamiwaza/services/context/pipeline/jobs/worker.py:251`) or transcription model (`kamiwaza/services/context/pipeline/jobs/worker.py:258`) is configured or auto-linked. The existing `ingestion.multimedia-extraction` document says no frame-level video analysis is claimed; this document claims it.

capabilities.title: Automatic specialist help in chat, with member pin and exclude policy
capabilities.summary:
- read my routing policy (Auto or a pinned agent, excluded agents, specialist help)
- set my routing policy
- read and set which agents each agent may call as sub-agents
- give a chat turn on Default, or on a pinned agent, a one-turn grant to consult one specialist the server picks
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
On by default. `AGENT_ROUTING_ENABLED` defaults to `True` (`src/kaizen/config.py:1164`), even though the comment above it (`src/kaizen/config.py:1161`) and the mount comment (`src/kaizen/member/app.py:272`) still say it is disabled by default. The code default is what ships. Administrators can switch it as a live setting (`src/kaizen/admin/catalog.py:282`). When it is off, the policy and sub-agent routes return not found (`src/kaizen/member/routes/routing_policy.py:40`, `src/kaizen/member/routes/agent_subagent_selection.py:90`), and no consult grant is issued (`src/kaizen/member/chat_routing.py:79`, `src/kaizen/member/chat_routing.py:122`).

Routing is server-side and rule-based in this build. A specialist is picked only when the message matches a reviewed routing tag on a routable chat agent and one agent scores highest; no match, or a tie, picks nobody (`src/kaizen/agents/routing.py:435`, `src/kaizen/agents/routing.py:447`). Candidates are capped at `AGENT_ROUTING_MAX_CANDIDATES`, default 5 (`src/kaizen/config.py:1166`). The consult path uses only this rule-based gate (`src/kaizen/member/chat_routing.py:394`). A model-based selector exists but is not wired into serving (`src/kaizen/agents/routing.py:540`), so do not claim that a model chooses the agent. Agents with web search or fetch tools are skipped unless the turn needs outside sources (`src/kaizen/agents/routing.py:416`).

On Default, or on the member's pinned agent when the policy allows specialist help (`src/kaizen/member/chat_routing.py:550`), a turn can get a one-turn grant to consult one specialist, and the serving agent keeps the answer (`src/kaizen/member/chat_routing.py:473`). The grant is issued only when the specialist adds a capability the serving agent lacks (`src/kaizen/member/chat_routing.py:380`). The specialist comes from the member's sub-agent choices for that agent plus any delegation links in the agent's reviewed definition, such as Default to the Web Researcher (`src/kaizen/member/chat_routing.py:308`, `src/kaizen/member/chat_routing.py:313`). The member's own sub-agent choices start empty (`src/kaizen/agents/routing.py:742`). A durable conversation keeps its selected agent and can only receive the one-turn grant (`src/kaizen/member/chat_routing.py:98`).

Exclusions narrow only the pinned path, which skips excluded agents (`src/kaizen/member/chat_routing.py:514`). A consult on Default ignores them: its pool is the sub-agent choices and reviewed delegation links (`src/kaizen/member/chat_routing.py:417`), and nothing on that path reads the exclusion list.

The policy belongs to the signed-in member; a request cannot name another owner (`src/kaizen/member/schemas.py:1911`). A pinned agent must be a chat agent the member can currently select, or the update is rejected (`src/kaizen/agents/routing.py:711`). Unknown excluded ids are dropped without an error (`src/kaizen/agents/routing.py:697`).

In the web app, the Agents screen's Use action saves the choice as a pin, or as Auto when the Default agent is chosen (`web/kaizen/src/lib/agentLaunch.ts:28`, `web/kaizen/src/lib/agents.ts:117`). The chat composer's Assist checkbox adds or removes an exclusion (`web/kaizen/src/lib/useComposerMenu.ts:411`). In Auto mode the web app sends the Default agent's id with each turn (`web/kaizen/src/lib/useComposerMenu.ts:95`), so an Auto turn in the web app runs on Default and can get at most the one-turn consult, and the Assist checkbox does not change which specialist Default may consult. A turn gets at most one specialist; planned multi-agent delegation is covered by `kaizen.multi-agent-orchestration`.

Not declared: the `auto` hand-off. The code can also hand a turn sent with agent `auto` to one specialist, which then owns the visible turn (`src/kaizen/agents/routing.py:5`), chosen from the member's selectable chat agents minus their exclusions (`src/kaizen/member/chat_routing.py:254`, `src/kaizen/agents/routing.py:237`). Nothing a member uses reaches it. The branch (`src/kaizen/member/chat_routing.py:70`) hands off only on the direct chat stream (`src/kaizen/member/member_chat_stream.py:56`), whose only caller outside tests is the inbound A2A runner (`src/kaizen/member/a2a.py:561`); a durable conversation keeps its selected agent (`src/kaizen/member/chat_routing.py:98`). Inbound A2A is off by default (`src/kaizen/config.py:1222`, `kamiwaza.json:146`). When it is on, a mapping made through the admin setup must resolve to a shared local chat agent (`src/kaizen/member/a2a_setup.py:343`), and every inbound call resolves the mapped id again as a selectable chat agent, answering 404 otherwise (`src/kaizen/member/routes/a2a.py:350`, `src/kaizen/member/routes/a2a.py:358`). A mapping can reach the branch only if `auto` resolves as an agent id; this batch did not establish whether any can.

The member proposal routes and the administrator routes both sit behind it and return not found when it is off (`src/kaizen/member/app.py:316`). Administrators can switch it as a live setting (`src/kaizen/admin/catalog.py:281`).

Review is API only. The web source contains administrator review and proposal panels (`web/kaizen/src/screens/agents/ManagePanel.tsx:401`, `web/kaizen/src/screens/agents/ProposalsPanel.tsx:130`), but no mounted screen renders them, and the old `/proposals` and `/review` paths redirect to the Agents hub (`web/kaizen/src/routes.tsx:113`, `web/kaizen/src/routes.tsx:114`). Not every agent needs approval. A member can create a private agent directly, and it is live at once with no approval (`src/kaizen/member/routes/agents.py:94`). This capability is the separate proposal lane that an administrator reviews.

Only the current workroom's Kaizen administrator can review (`src/kaizen/member/authz.py:169`). Approval is the only route that makes a proposed agent or package active: a proposal becomes approved only in the two approve mutations (`src/kaizen/agents/studio/lifecycle_agent_mutations.py:342`, `src/kaizen/agents/studio/lifecycle_package_mutations.py:215`), which only the admin approve routes call (`src/kaizen/member/routes/ops_agents.py:234`, `src/kaizen/member/routes/ops_agents.py:256`). Members see and change only their own proposals (`src/kaizen/member/routes/studio.py:209`, `src/kaizen/agents/studio/proposals.py:317`). A proposal that changes an existing agent requires the member to own that agent or be an administrator (`src/kaizen/member/routes/studio.py:231`). Submit re-validates the content and moves a draft or rejected proposal to pending approval (`src/kaizen/agents/studio/proposals.py:495`). The sandbox test is owner-only, read-only and not saved to chat history (`src/kaizen/member/routes/studio.py:360`); search presets cannot be tested there (`src/kaizen/member/routes/studio.py:376`).

conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:

The route records the turn id it is given (`src/kaizen/member/routes/feedback.py:48`) and does not look the turn up. The only route is a `POST` that records a vote (`src/kaizen/member/routes/feedback.py:67`); there is no route to change or withdraw one.

capabilities.title: Member chat compression controls
capabilities.summary:
- read my compression settings and what is in effect
- set my compression settings: a master switch plus Tool-result compression, Plain-speak and Prompt trim
- view compression statistics for me and for a conversation I can read
- reset my compression statistics
- compact a conversation I own, with optional guidance, and follow its progress
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
Available by default; each member opts in. `MEMBER_COMPRESSION_ENABLED` defaults to `True` (`src/kaizen/config.py:1886`), and so do the three per-control flags (`src/kaizen/config.py:1887`, `src/kaizen/config.py:1888`, `src/kaizen/config.py:1891`). A member's settings start with everything off (`src/kaizen/domain/compression.py:36`). A control takes effect only when the deployment allows it and the member has turned on both the master switch and that control (`src/kaizen/domain/compression.py:158`). When `MEMBER_COMPRESSION_ENABLED` is off, the settings and statistics routes return not found (`src/kaizen/member/app.py:498`). Administrators can switch it as a live setting (`src/kaizen/admin/catalog.py:242`).

Where the three controls take effect was traced through the Pi agent adapter (`src/kaizen/agents/adapters/pi_core.py:48`, `src/kaizen/agents/adapters/pi_run_loop.py:740`); other agent runtimes were not checked.

What each control does:

- Tool-result compression applies to code-execution output. The sandbox worker runs a pinned RTK pass over captured stdout and stderr and returns the raw output beside a compressed copy (`src/kaizen/sandbox/rpc.py:229`).
- Plain-speak turns on the bundled third-party Caveman skill at its default intensity for visible prose (`src/kaizen/services/plain_speak_directive.py:24`). Its activation text tells the model that the skill must not change tool use, citations or approvals (`src/kaizen/services/plain_speak_directive.py:32`), and that a toggle change applies from the next turn (`src/kaizen/services/plain_speak_directive.py:30`); these are instructions to the model, not separately enforced. The skill is pinned to an upstream commit and MIT-licensed (`src/kaizen/skills/caveman/PROVENANCE.md:5`, `src/kaizen/skills/caveman/PROVENANCE.md:9`).
- Prompt trim removes listed filler from the copy of a message sent to the model; the transcript keeps the member's own words (`src/kaizen/services/prompt_fluff_stripper.py:4`). Unusual hedging survives because the rule list is fixed (`src/kaizen/services/prompt_fluff_stripper.py:8`).

No savings figure is guaranteed. Token savings are reported as estimates (`src/kaizen/member/routes/compression.py:127`), and Plain-speak's eligible size is itself estimated (`src/kaizen/member/routes/compression.py:123`). The 65% figure in the bundled skill text is the upstream author's claim (`src/kaizen/skills/caveman/SKILL.md:4`), not a Kaizen measurement. Reset clears only the member-level statistics (`src/kaizen/member/routes/compression.py:340`). Conversation statistics appear only for conversations the member can read (`src/kaizen/member/routes/compression.py:279`).

Manual compaction does not depend on the compression flag. It lives on the conversation routes, which are mounted without it (`src/kaizen/member/app.py:238`), and it is owner-only: shared readers and other members get not found (`src/kaizen/member/manual_compaction.py:56`). It runs in the background and streams progress events (`src/kaizen/member/routes/conversations.py:341`).

In the web app, Settings > Compression holds the switches (`web/kaizen/src/routes.tsx:126`), and chat offers a "Compact this chat" command, `/compact` (`web/kaizen/src/lib/commands.ts:68`, `web/kaizen/src/lib/manualCompactionCommand.ts:1`), which starts a compaction (`web/kaizen/src/screens/chat/use-manual-compaction-command.tsx:170`).

capabilities.title: Create and configure custom agents in Kaizen Legacy
capabilities.summary:
- **Analyst-created, named agents.** `AgentService.create` (`kamiwaza_sdk/services/kaizen.py:675`) creates an agent with a name, a model and optional instructions; `list` (`:737`) enumerates them per workroom. Kaizen Legacy serves both at `/api/agents` (`backend/app/api/v1/agents.py:686`, `backend/app/api/v1/agents.py:739`).
- **Skills bind to agents.** `bind_skill` (`:755`) attaches a skill from the library, which is what makes an agent specialised rather than a renamed default assistant. Kaizen Legacy accepts only a published skill and answers 404 for any other (`backend/app/api/v1/agents.py:835`, `backend/app/api/v1/agents.py:862`). The library itself is a separate claim (`skills.skills-library`) and can be true while this one is not.
- **A documented creation path in the user guide**, so this is a supported analyst workflow rather than an SDK-only affordance (`docs/extensions/kaizen/kaizen-user-guide.md:54` in `kamiwaza-docs` at `63317db3`).
conditions: Kaizen Legacy, App Garden catalog identity `kaizen-legacy`, version 2.1.4, on Kamiwaza 1.3.0 or later. A separate app from `kaizen` 0.6.1, which creates agents through a different contract.
Agents are managed per workroom, so an agent belongs to a workroom rather than to the platform globally.
Binding a skill to an agent presupposes the skill exists in the skills library and is published.
limits:
- **This is Kaizen Legacy, not the app named `kaizen`.** The product is App Garden catalog identity `kaizen-legacy`, display name "Kaizen (Legacy)", version 2.1.4, for Kamiwaza 1.3.0 or later (`kamiwaza.json:2`, `kamiwaza.json:4`, `kamiwaza.json:5` in `kamiwaza-extensions-kaizen` at `82a7bb3c`). The bundled catalog lists the same name and version (`charts/core/files/catalog/garden/v3/apps.json:1231`, `charts/core/files/catalog/garden/v3/apps.json:1237` in `deploy` at `aa51ca9a`). The app named `kaizen` in that catalog is version 0.6.1 (`charts/core/files/catalog/garden/v3/apps.json:192`, `charts/core/files/catalog/garden/v3/apps.json:194`) and is a separate product built from `kamiwaza-extensions-tomo`. The catalog pins Legacy's images by digest under the revision label `develop` (`charts/core/files/catalog/garden/v3/apps.json:1233`); nothing read here shows those images were built from the cited source commit.
- **The two products create agents differently, and the SDK keeps them apart.** `AgentService.create` is the Legacy contract: a flat body whose `agent_config.llm` binds the model. The SDK states that the app named `kaizen` rejects that body and takes `create_canonical` instead, which carries no per-agent model (`kamiwaza_sdk/services/kaizen.py:610`, `kamiwaza_sdk/services/kaizen.py:622`). So "chooses its model" is true of Kaizen Legacy and is not claimed for `kaizen`. Agent creation on `kaizen` is not this document's claim.
- **Skill binding was traced in Kaizen Legacy only.** The route `bind_skill` calls exists in Kaizen Legacy. A text search for `skill-bindings` under `src/kaizen` in `kamiwaza-extensions-tomo` at `260e50d0`, the commit the catalog names for `kaizen` 0.6.1, found no such route. That is a bounded search, not proof of absence.
- **Skills are attached after the agent exists.** Kaizen Legacy rejects `skill_bindings` sent in the create request (`backend/app/api/v1/agents.py:373`) and answers 409 when a skill is already attached (`backend/app/api/v1/agents.py:851`).
- **Creating and binding need workroom write access** (`backend/app/api/v1/agents.py:700`, `backend/app/api/v1/agents.py:845`); listing is filtered to the caller's workroom scope (`backend/app/api/v1/agents.py:756`).
- **The user guide does not say which app it describes.** It says "Kaizen" throughout. The steps it walks through — Basic Configuration with a name, a model and instructions, then Skills, MCP servers, Security Policy, and Review & Create — are the steps of Kaizen Legacy's agent wizard (`frontend/app/components/agent-creation-wizard.tsx:47`).
- **How an agent behaves at run time is not claimed.** How instructions are applied, how the chosen model is used, and how a bound skill is invoked were not traced, and this document makes no claim about them.
- **Local agent creation is the whole claim.** The three exclusions above are the parts most often assumed to come with "custom agents". This document does not claim them. They are unestablished rather than denied.
- **No claim is made about what an agent produces.** Creating and configuring an agent is established by the sources; the quality, grounding, or citation behavior of its output is not this capability's claim.

capabilities.title: Daily model-token budget per member
capabilities.summary:
- set the per-member daily cap (through the settings update route, which `kaizen.admin-settings-console` declares)
- check a member's usage before a direct model call
- refuse the call once the cap is reached
conditions: LLM_PER_USER_DAILY_TOKENS set to a positive number; it ships as 0, which disables the check. Changing it live needs the config store on and a Kaizen administrator.
limits:
**Off by default.** `LLM_PER_USER_DAILY_TOKENS` defaults to 0 in settings ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/config.py:329](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/config.py#L329)) and in the install manifest ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/kamiwaza.json:135](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/kamiwaza.json#L135)), whose description reads "0 (the default) allows unlimited daily tokens" ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/kamiwaza.json:593](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/kamiwaza.json#L593)). With a zero cap the check returns before it reads the usage ledger, so a member's daily model use is unbounded until an operator sets a positive number ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/llm_gateway/policy.py:99](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/llm_gateway/policy.py#L99)).

Kaizen administrators can change the cap as a live setting in the Rate limits group of the admin Settings screen ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/admin/catalog.py:598](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/admin/catalog.py#L598)). The settings routes require a Kaizen administrator, and a setting is editable only when the config store is on. The packaged install turns the config store on ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/kamiwaza.json:174](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/kamiwaza.json#L174)); the bare settings default is off ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/config.py:1667](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/config.py#L1667)).

Usage is the sum of prompt and response tokens on successful calls in Kaizen's LLM audit ledger since the start of the current UTC day ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/repositories/llm_audit.py:41](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/repositories/llm_audit.py#L41)). The check takes a per-member advisory lock, then compares usage already recorded with the cap before the call runs ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/llm_gateway/policy.py:108](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/llm_gateway/policy.py#L108)). It does not reserve the cost of the call about to run, so one call can take a member past the cap. Embedding calls made by Kaizen's system requester, which it uses for connector and uploaded-document ingestion, skip the check; the system requester's other calls and a member's embedding calls do not ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/llm_gateway/policy.py:101](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/llm_gateway/policy.py#L101)).

Setting a positive cap also switches on fixed in-process daily caps per request category (50,000 or 100,000 tokens) that are counted per process, not per member, and are not configurable ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/llm_gateway/policy.py:14](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/llm_gateway/policy.py#L14)). They are a side effect of the setting and are not declared here as an operation.

The check runs on Kaizen's direct model gateway ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/llm_gateway/factory.py:136](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/llm_gateway/factory.py#L136)) and on the model proxy used by the agent runtime, which answers an over-cap request with HTTP 429 `budget_exceeded` and writes a `budget_exceeded` audit row before any provider call ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/member/routes/pi_model_proxy.py:303](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/member/routes/pi_model_proxy.py#L303)). How that refusal reads to the member inside a chat turn was not traced for this document, and this document does not establish that every model call in Kaizen passes through these two paths.

The cap counts tokens, per member, per UTC day. It is not a currency spending cap and not a total across all members. It is separate from the platform's delegated-model caps (delegation.brokered-resource-access) and from the platform's activity records (platform.usage-and-audit).

capabilities.title: Governed platform inspection and demo actions
capabilities.summary:
- inspect
- preview
- apply
conditions: KAMIWAZA_SDK_TOOLS_ENABLED on (the default), an agent granted these tools, and a member turn carrying the forwarded platform identity. Whether apply prompts depends on the member's resolved approval mode.
limits:
No arbitrary SDK call, URL, credentials, delete or raw payload: both tools validate a closed request schema and dispatch only to reviewed operations.

**Apply is always bound to a preview.** An apply request must carry the environment binding and the preview digest that a prior preview returned; the schema rejects an apply without both ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/agents/kamiwaza_sdk_contract.py:389](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/agents/kamiwaza_sdk_contract.py#L389)). Before anything else, the tool recomputes both and refuses with `environment_changed` or `preview_changed` when the platform address, the workroom or any part of the desired state differs from what was previewed ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/agents/kamiwaza_sdk_tools.py:772](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/agents/kamiwaza_sdk_tools.py#L772)). No approval mode waives this.

**Whether a member is asked first is policy-resolved, and the shipped default does not ask.** Apply declares that it needs confirmation, and the tool refuses with `approval_required` unless the runtime marks the call confirmed ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/agents/kamiwaza_sdk_tools.py:321](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/agents/kamiwaza_sdk_tools.py#L321)). The runtime sets that mark from the member's resolved approval mode, never from model arguments or request payloads ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/llm_tools/protocol.py:40](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/llm_tools/protocol.py#L40)):

- **Never ask**, the built-in workspace default ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/config.py:1177](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/config.py#L1177)): apply runs without a prompt and its receipt reads `approval: not_required`.
- The default-ask and **Ask before writes** modes: the member sees an approval card naming the environment, workroom and change; once approved, the receipt reads `approval: consumed`.
- **Read-only**: apply is denied.

Changing the workspace approval default changes inherited behavior only. Member, agent, turn or task choices can still resolve to **Never ask**; this source does not establish a hard always-review ceiling. Apply also runs only for the member whose turn requested it, and only through Kaizen's interactive approval surface; without that surface it refuses with `approval_unavailable`.

Generic Core/MCP exact tools still opt-in; empty allowlist fail-closed. The whole tool family can be switched off with `KAMIWAZA_SDK_TOOLS_ENABLED` ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/config.py:1702](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/config.py#L1702)).

capabilities.title: Prebuilt specialist agents
capabilities.summary:
- provision the bundled agents at startup
- list them in the Agents gallery
- choose one for a chat turn
conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
On by default. At startup Kaizen provisions every bundle in its agent-bundle directory unless AGENT_BUNDLES_ENABLED is false (src/kaizen/agents/bundles.py:533, src/kaizen/config.py:2014). The image copies the four bundles into that directory (docker/Dockerfile:143), and the service runs the loader before it starts serving (src/kaizen/main.py:322). Loading is best-effort: a bundle that fails is logged and skipped, and startup continues (src/kaizen/agents/bundles.py:543). If an agent with the same name already exists and the bundle did not create it, the bundle leaves it alone and does not add its own (src/kaizen/agents/bundles.py:433).

Bundle agents are created shared and protected (src/kaizen/agents/bundles.py:482, src/kaizen/agents/bundles.py:490). conditions: The required configuration, services and permissions described below must be present.
limits:
This is Kaizen Legacy: App Garden catalog identity `kaizen-legacy`, display name "Kaizen (Legacy)", version 2.1.4, for Kamiwaza 1.3.0 or later (`kamiwaza.json:2`, `kamiwaza.json:4`, `kamiwaza.json:5`). The catalog pins Legacy's images by digest under the revision label `develop` (`charts/core/files/catalog/garden/v3/apps.json:1233`); nothing read here shows those images were built from the source commit this document cites.

The primary Kaizen LLM gateway at source commit `260e50d0` states that it does not apply a redaction policy to model input (`src/kaizen/llm_gateway/policy.py:104` in `kamiwaza-extensions-tomo`). This statement concerns the gateway; it is not an exhaustive exclusion of browser-side checks on other surfaces.

Privacy Guard is off by default. When neither the conversation nor its agent sets a valid mode, the effective mode is `off` (`backend/app/api/v1/conversations.py:2166`). A conversation override wins. Otherwise the agent's `agent_context.privacy_filter` mode applies (`backend/app/api/v1/conversations.py:2157`), which the agent wizard writes when the chosen mode is not off (`frontend/app/components/agent-creation-wizard.tsx:608`). The backend accepts only `off`, `warn` and `redact` (`backend/app/api/v1/conversations.py:1989`, `backend/app/api/v1/conversations.py:2020`). While a conversation's settings are loading, or if they fail to load, the chat page uses warn mode (`frontend/app/conversations/[id]/page.tsx:486`, `frontend/app/conversations/[id]/page.tsx:488`).

The check runs in the browser, in the message box's send handler (`frontend/app/components/chat/message-input.tsx:106`). The settings panel calls it a light browser-side review (`frontend/app/components/chat/conversation-settings-panel.tsx:525`). The backend stores and returns the mode, and a search of the backend Python at this revision found no code that applies it to message text. So a client that calls the message API directly is not checked; that is inferred from where the check lives, not run.

Detection is a fixed list of regular expressions (`frontend/lib/privacy-guard.ts:29`): email addresses, US-style phone numbers, SSNs written as `123-45-6789`, IPv4 addresses, `sk-` keys and several key, token, secret and password patterns (`frontend/lib/privacy-guard.ts:49`). It is not data-loss prevention and will miss identifiers outside those patterns. Only the typed text is scanned; attached images are sent unchanged (`frontend/app/components/chat/message-input.tsx:115`). In warn mode the user can still send the original text (`frontend/app/components/chat/message-input.tsx:370`).

The settings routes are `GET` and `PATCH /api/conversations/{conversation_id}/settings` (`backend/app/main.py:220`, `backend/app/api/v1/conversations.py:1918`, `backend/app/api/v1/conversations.py:2735`). Changing a conversation's mode requires ownership of the conversation (`backend/app/api/v1/conversations.py:2806`). Those two settings change the role check and leave the ownership check alone. When `KAMIWAZA_USE_AUTH` is set to a false value the role check is skipped (`backend/app/utils/workroom_access.py:60`, `backend/app/utils/workroom_access.py:169`). When the legacy-header setting is on, a request that carries no role is let through (`backend/app/utils/workroom_access.py:130`). In the Global workroom no role is needed (`backend/app/utils/workroom_access.py:172`). This is read from source; no deployment's settings were inspected.

capabilities.title: Shared project workspaces
capabilities.summary:
- create
- list
- update
- archive
- invite
- link-library-item
conditions: PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ENABLED and SHARED_CHAT_COLLABORATION_ENABLED on (both default to true); creating a Project requires a signed-in member, not pre-existing Project membership; operations on an existing Project require active membership with the necessary role.
limits:
The Project routes are mounted only when `PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ENABLED` and `SHARED_CHAT_COLLABORATION_ENABLED` are both on; both default to true ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/config.py:1800](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/config.py#L1800), [kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/config.py:1784](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/config.py#L1784)). Updating a Project and inviting to it need the owner role; linking, unlinking and changing a link's access need the writer role.

**Linking is not copying.** A link stores a pointer to the member's own Library item. The source row is not duplicated, and deleting or unlinking the source removes the Project view.

**A shared pointer lends a read, and only its owner can issue one.** For artifacts, documents and prompts, a link is stored `shared` when the linking member's share-new-items preference is on, which it is until that member turns it off ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/repositories/project_library_pointers.py:133](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/repositories/project_library_pointers.py#L133)). A shared pointer lets the Project's active members read that one item. The read holds only while three facts are true at query time: the member who made the link owns the source item, the pointer is still `shared`, and the reader's Project membership is still active ([kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/repositories/project_grants.py:46](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/repositories/project_grants.py#L46), [kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/src/kaizen/repositories/project_grants.py:80](https://github.com/kamiwaza-internal/kamiwaza-extensions-tomo/blob/13c72eb16be443eb09cbe079648f6aabd71f4060/src/kaizen/repositories/project_grants.py#L80)). A member cannot lend an item they do not own.

**The read is revocable.** Setting the pointer to private, unlinking it, deleting the source, or the reader leaving or being removed from the Project withdraws the read on the next query. Only the member who made a link can change its access.

**Nothing beyond the read is lent.** A Project grant does not transfer ownership or confer edit, rename, publish, delete, re-share or wider Library access; writes stay owner-scoped. A pointer to any other kind (a task, an agent, another Project) stays private and is resolved under each viewer's own access. Agent turns in a Project chat still resolve models, tools, credentials and approvals for the member who started the turn.

limits:

The catalog pins Legacy's images by digest under the revision label `develop` (`charts/core/files/catalog/garden/v3/apps.json:1233`); nothing read here shows those images were built from the source commit this document cites.

Recipes are on by default, with no feature flag. The recipe routes are mounted under `/api/recipes` (`backend/app/main.py:241`, `backend/app/api/v1/recipes.py:34`). The lookup tool is added to every OpenHands agent when a conversation is created (`backend/app/services/conversation_manager.py:1443`) and when it resumes (`backend/app/services/conversation_manager.py:2897`), and a per-conversation tool selection keeps it (`backend/app/services/conversation_manager.py:1157`). A tool-call result has a Save as Recipe button (`frontend/app/search/page.tsx:641`), only tool-call events can be saved (`frontend/app/search/page.tsx:184`), and the Recipes tab lists what was saved (`frontend/app/search/page.tsx:712`).

Saving replaces sensitive values with `[REDACTED]` (`backend/app/utils/recipe_payload.py:9`). That covers values under keys such as password, secret, token, API key, authorization, cookie and private key (`backend/app/utils/recipe_payload.py:13`), and strings that look like bearer tokens, `sk-` or `rk-` keys, AWS access keys or JWTs (`backend/app/utils/recipe_payload.py:24`). The arguments and the result are each capped at 128 KB (`backend/app/utils/recipe_payload.py:10`), and a larger payload gets HTTP 413 (`backend/app/api/v1/recipes.py:54`). After saving, only the name and notes can change (`backend/app/api/v1/recipes.py:154`, `backend/app/schemas/recipe.py:18`).

Visibility follows the workroom. In a shared workroom every member sees the workroom's recipes; in the Global workroom each user sees only their own (`backend/app/utils/resource_scope.py:41`, `backend/app/utils/resource_scope.py:42`). Rename and delete use the same filter, so in a shared workroom any member with a write-capable role (owner, editor, contributor or member) can change or remove another member's recipe (`backend/app/api/v1/recipes.py:188`, `backend/app/utils/workroom_access.py:34`). Saving, renaming and deleting pass through the workroom write check (`backend/app/api/v1/recipes.py:71`, `backend/app/api/v1/recipes.py:155`, `backend/app/api/v1/recipes.py:188`); listing and viewing do not.

The agent lookup needs a tool name or a keyword (`backend/app/api/v1/agent_context.py:1449`). The keyword matches recipe names, notes and arguments (`backend/app/api/v1/agent_context.py:1473`). It searches the conversation's workroom, and in the Global workroom only the recipes of the conversation's user (`backend/app/api/v1/agent_context.py:1461`, `backend/app/utils/resource_scope.py:41`) and returns at most the 20 newest matches (`backend/app/api/v1/agent_context.py:1481`). The text the agent reads cuts arguments and results at 500 characters each (`backend/agent_tools/recipe_lookup/schemas.py:63`). A recipe returns the stored arguments and result as saved (`backend/app/api/v1/agent_context.py:1491`, `backend/app/api/v1/agent_context.py:1492`). Nothing re-runs or checks them, so a recipe does not show that the call still works.

State is ephemeral and kept in Valkey (src/kaizen/member/conversation_presence.py:1, src/kaizen/config.py:1845). capabilities.title: Discover and download models from model hubs
capabilities.summary:
- **Hub search with graceful degradation.** `POST /models/search/` searches the requested hubs for an authenticated caller. Hub rate limiting does not fail the whole search: the platform runs Hugging Face API calls in a dedicated thread pool and returns results together with hub-status degradation info, so a rate-limited hub yields partial results with an error indicator rather than an error.
- **File-level inspection before download.** The SDK's `search_models` loads each result's file list and detects the quantization variants present (`available_quantizations`), so the operator chooses artifacts — a specific GGUF quant for CPU hardware, `.safetensors` for GPU serving — rather than blindly pulling a repository.
- **Quantization-aware download initiation.** `POST /models/download/` initiates the download and returns the initiation result plus the model-file ids being downloaded. The SDK's `initiate_model_download(repo_id, quantization=...)` selects files for the requested quantization when a repository carries multiple variants (default `q6_k`), downloads all files when it does not, skips files that are already satisfied locally, and — when the requested quantization does not exist — fails with the list of quantizations that do.
- **Trackable and cancellable downloads.** `GET /model_files/download_status/` reports per-file download status; the SDK's `check_download_status` presents percentage complete, throughput, remaining and elapsed time per file. An in-flight download can be cancelled via `DELETE /model_files/{model_file_id}/download`.
- **Access control on acquisition.** Download initiation is authorized per model and tenant on the server side; the downloading user is assigned ownership/viewer access under relationship-based access control, and models pulled from the Hugging Face Hub get a public viewer tuple so authorized users can discover them without manual tuple edits.
- **Downloaded files are cached and registered.** Artifacts land in a local cache directory; subsequent requests for the same model do not re-download. Once downloaded, files are registered in Kamiwaza and become available for deployment.
conditions: The Kamiwaza control plane has outbound access to the source hub (Hugging Face Hub or a configured registry).
The caller is authenticated; download initiation is additionally authorized per model.
limits:
- Search is discovery metadata only — it is authenticated but deliberately not object-guarded; per-model authorization applies at download time, not search time.
- Admission is enforced at initiation: object-store admission failures and insufficient disk space are rejected as client errors when the download is requested, not discovered later as a hung transfer.
- Models are identified by hub repository id (for example `meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct`); gated or licensed repositories are subject to the hub's own access rules on the credentials the platform uses.
